Skin cancer, on the other hand, will increase, although more and more people know they need to protect themselves well. This is because the effect of now applying sunscreen better only becomes visible in the figures after years. In 2045, skin cancer will be the most common form of cancer for both men and women, IKNL writes in the report. Among men, prostate cancer is currently still the most common type of cancer, and among women it is breast cancer. Tanmaxxing. Although changes in lifestyle trends have not been included in the figures, IKNL does point to new worrying developments in its research. "Consider the increasing use of nicotine products among young girls, or online challenges in which young people deliberately expose themselves to the sun unprotected for as long as possible". For example tanmaxxing, a social media trend in which people try to become as tanned as possible. According to Schilte-Praagman, about 30 percent of cancer cases are related to risk factors we can influence, such as lifestyle. "Eating healthily, not smoking, not drinking too much and getting enough exercise help. In addition, it is important to protect your skin against UV radiation. It is not only the responsibility of the individual; we must also work together to ensure that the living environment is healthy and that people can make healthy choices." Just bad luck. That does not alter the fact that people who live healthily can also get cancer. In many cases it is a matter of bad luck and other factors play a role. Schilte-Praagman: "But a healthy lifestyle can certainly help reduce the risk of cancer." Due to ageing and the associated rise in the number of cancer diagnoses, the number of people who die of cancer will also increase. But the risk of dying of cancer has been decreasing for years, a trend that is expected to continue over the next twenty years. "Thirty years ago, about half of cancer patients were still alive five years after diagnosis. Today that percentage is 71 percent", concludes Schilte-Paagman. This is due, among other things, to improvements in treatments, (early) diagnostics and other factors, such as healthier living.

title: Houthis attack airports in Yemen and Saudi Arabia
lead: The Houthis have attacked an airport in Aden, in southern Yemen, with missiles and drones. Nothing is yet known about damage or casualties. A missile reportedly landed close to the runway, a few minutes before an aircraft from Cairo was to land there. That aircraft was just in time diverted to Saudi Arabia. As a precaution, two aircraft that were standing on the runway were moved. A missile was also reportedly fired at Saudi Arabia. It was intercepted and destroyed north of the capital Riyadh. Saudi Arabia supports the Yemeni army in the fight against the Houthis. Yesterday two airports in Saudi Arabia were also attacked by the Houthis. At least three people were injured in that attack. The Houthis have not confirmed that they are behind the attack on the airport in Aden. A military spokesperson did say that the airport of Riyadh was attacked with "multiple drones." Strait Earlier this week the Yemeni government army launched a counteroffensive, in which, according to the minister of Information, the important Bab al-Mandab strait was recaptured. It had been occupied by the Houthis last month. The aim of operation "Dawn of Yemen" is to end the Houthi coup in Yemen and recapture occupied government institutions. The Houthis still hold a large part of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. They are supported by Iran. These are verified images of the government army's offensive earlier this week in Yemen at the Bab al-Mandab strait:

title: Interest on student debt rises sharply for a large group of former students
lead: Next year, the interest on student finance and student debt will rise for students and 250,000 former students. For some of them, the interest will rise by almost 1 percentage point, from 2.29 percent to 3.28 percent. How much the interest rises depends on whether you are still studying and under which repayment rules you fall. Most current students have to repay their debt over 35 years. For them, the interest rises much less: from 2.33 percent to 2.70 percent. Most people who have since graduated fall under the 15-year repayment rules. For them, a new interest rate is set every five years. Five years ago they still paid 0 percent interest. Now it is 3.28 percent. Why does the interest differ? The interest on student loans is based on the interest the government pays. The rates differ this much because they are calculated differently. For the 15-year rule there is one reference date, while for the 35-year rule the average interest over a longer period is used. Earlier this week it became known that total student debt has decreased for the first time in a long time. However, the number of graduates with a very high student debt, above 50,000 euros, has increased considerably. This is partly explained by the loan system, which has since been abolished. Voices have long been calling to lower the interest for this group of students, also known as the 'bad luck generation'. D66, VVD and CDA also want this: in their coalition agreement they agreed to set the interest for students at a maximum of 2.5 percent. So far, no plans for this have been made public. <entity id="org:dienst-uitvoering-onderwijs">DUO</entity>, the organisation responsible for student finance, takes a person's income into account when repaying student debt. Those who earn little have to repay less. The debt that remains after a repayment period is ultimately forgiven.

title: Heavy Russian attack on Ukraine: 20 dead, including 4 children
lead: Russian attacks on various locations in Ukraine have killed at least twenty people overnight. In an attack on an apartment building in the northern city of Pryloeky, at least fourteen people died, including four children. The attack also injured fifty people, including seven children. Video footage shows rescuers still searching for people under the rubble. Ukrainian President Zelensky speaks of heavy attacks on the country. "One of the main targets was our energy infrastructure. The Russians wanted to deal a painful blow", he writes. "In total, seventy missiles were launched, many of them ballistic, as well as Shaheds. Unfortunately only a few of them were shot down. Russian ballistic missiles remain the biggest challenge." Ukraine has carried out counterattacks on four targets, in the regions of Perm, Samara and Astrachan. Among other things, two oil facilities were hit. The new generation of Russian Shahed drones is even faster and more destructive and sharpens the balance on the battlefield: The dead fell among others in Kyiv, in Pryloeky and in the Poltava region. The nearby regions of Charkiv and Dnipropetrovsk were also targeted. There is damage to homes and factories, Ukrainian authorities report. The Ukrainian air force says that Russia fired not 70 but 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and five ballistic missiles overnight. The Russian Ministry of Defence confirms that its armed forces carried out a massive attack on facilities in Kyiv and other regions. Targets were, according to Russia, among others the Ukrainian defence company Fire Point, where Ukraine would store its Flamingo cruise missiles and drones for medium and long range. Ballistic missile: last week President Zelensky announced that Ukraine had for the first time fired a ballistic missile produced by Fire Point. In an interview with news agency Reuters last week, Zelensky said he expected the company to have an FP-9 missile with a greater range ready by autumn; according to him this ballistic missile has a range up to and including Moscow. Ukraine has for months been suffering a serious shortage of air defence, particularly to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles. Therefore Zelensky has repeatedly asked his allies to supply new weapons. That need is growing now that Russian air attacks are becoming ever more intense. The European Commission announces today that Ukraine will receive 1.24 billion euros to purchase drones and anti-drone equipment with it. "Russia is conducting a deliberate strategy of terror. Europe is taking its responsibility and others must also step up their support", says Commission President Von der Leyen.

title: French police temporarily stop using stun grenades at schoolchildren's protests
lead: French police will not use stun grenades at the schoolchildren's protests for the coming period, says the Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, Nuñez. A stun grenade is used to blind or stun people with a loud bang and a flash of light. The decision comes after a 15-year-old boy lost his hand at a demonstration in the city of Lens. The mayor of Wingles, where the boy lives, says the teenager's left hand has been amputated. He also had a transplant on his right hand and suffered injuries to his face and chest. Since last week, protests against problems in education have been held at schools across France. Schoolchildren are demonstrating against, among other things, overdue maintenance of school buildings, classes that are too large, school days that are too long and the teacher shortage in France. Arrested or thrown? It is still unclear exactly what went wrong in Lens. Riot police were called when the demonstration there reportedly turned into riots, according to French authorities. French media, citing a police source, write that riot police threw a stun grenade and that the boy wanted to throw it back. The grenade then reportedly exploded in his hand. Eyewitnesses say the stun grenade was thrown and landed directly in the hand of the 15-year-old. So he would not have picked it up. An investigation has been launched into the incident. The use of stun grenades is being suspended "until the truth has come to light", Nuñez told the French branch of RTL. Multiple incidents This is not the first incident since the protests began. So far 215 schoolchildren have been injured. Another boy, for example, broke his jaw last week when he was hit in the face by a tear gas grenade. That case is also being investigated. Nuñez previously said that eighteen investigations are underway into violent incidents. The minister has called on police to use proportionate force. On the petition platform for the French parliament, a petition has been started to ban the use of weapons and grenades at demonstrations. It has already collected thousands of signatures. Demonstrations announced Today there do not appear to be any large protests planned. Many schools are simply open today. Yesterday French Prime Minister Lecornu said there would be three days without lessons at schools. At that time it was unclear whether schools would follow this. According to the Ministry of Education, lessons at 86 percent of secondary schools continue as normal today. At 528 schools, lessons have been partly or completely suspended. However, it seems the protests will not stop yet. One of the largest unions in France, CGT, said there are plans to continue demonstrating tomorrow. Lecornu will give a speech this evening about the ongoing unrest and demonstrations.

title: Cabinet and social partners had a good first conversation
lead: The cabinet and employers and employees have had a good conversation after months of action. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> called it a first conversation in which people also laughed now and then. The atmosphere was good, agreed among others FNV chair Spekman and VNO-NCW chair Van Oostrom. The urgency to keep talking was felt by everyone. Jetten said that the trade unions confirmed at the Catshuis that the actions have been suspended for the time being. Talks will continue in a few weeks. 'No savings target' That should ultimately lead to a social agreement, but that is not yet within reach. "The negotiations still have to really start", according to Jetten. He wants a number of agreements to have been made by spring. FNV chair Spekman said that in those negotiations there is no target to achieve a certain amount of savings. According to him, the cabinet agreed to that at the table. He wants to talk about improvements to benefits for unemployment or incapacity for work and does not rule out that this will yield money. "But we do not have to meet an assignment." Bill at other ministries According to <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">minister Vijlbrief</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity>, the reform of the WIA, the benefit for people who are ill, is "really the big thing". The cabinet has taken the cuts to social security off the table, but they are not entirely gone. If the cabinet and the unions do not reach agreement, the bill will land with other ministries. Especially the Ministry of Education would then have to bear a large part of that bill.

title: 'Phoenix planet' discovered, formed from the remains of a dead star
lead: British astronomers have discovered a new type of celestial body: a planet orbiting a burnt-out star. The discoverers call it a phoenix planet, after the mythological bird that rises from its own ashes. The discovery may tell us more about the distant future of our own solar system. Scientists from the University of Warwick describe their discovery around the star HS 0209+0832, in the constellation Cetus, in the journal Nature Astronomy. It is a white dwarf, about 250 light years from Earth. A white dwarf is what remains when a star has lost most of its mass at the end of its life. The sun also faces this fate eventually: the star first swells and swallows the nearest planets such as Venus, Mercury and perhaps Earth. Most of the material is eventually flung into space and forms an expanding nebula around a core that barely shines anymore. Clumped together again The new research shows that this state does not have to be the end point of the life cycle of a planetary system. At HS 0209+0832, the material from the planetary nebula has apparently clumped together again into a new planet, just as happened billions of years earlier when the star formed. A 'second clutch' for this star, then. The scientists were able to rule out that it was a planet that had formed earlier, because traces of heavy materials such as the metals zinc, copper and niobium were found. These are all elements that form when a star dies. Recycled The new planet is a gas giant slightly larger than Jupiter. It orbits its star every 4.4 days at only 4 percent of the distance between the sun and the earth. This means the planet is uninhabitable due to the radiation from its parent star. Because the distance is so small, the white dwarf also gradually strips away the outer layer of the planet. Earlier, similar planets made from recycled material had already been found around pulsars, the end point of stars that are considerably larger than the sun. However, these occur much less often in the universe than stars like the sun. That such new planets could also form in that category was not yet known.

title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry for research into mirror-image molecules
lead: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to Frenchman Henri Kagan and Japanese scientist Kenso Soai. They researched the discovery of "non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". In somewhat more understandable language: some molecules exist in two variants that are mirror images of each other. If molecules are rotated one way, they can have a different effect than when they are rotated the other way. And this while they have the same composition. Scientists call this left-handed and right-handed. For example, there is a cough suppressant which, when the molecules are reversed, is a painkiller. "Medicines can have the desired effect one way, but the other way they may have no effect or even be harmful," the committee states . Kagan (95) and Soai (76) have discovered how exactly this works. Kagan took the first step with his research from 1986, in which he managed to manipulate chemical reactions. Soai built on that. In 1995 he discovered a chemical reaction in which only one of the two mirror images was formed. In the series Breaking Bad, chemistry teacher Walter White also once explained this principle: According to the Nobel committee, Kagan and Soai have found a solution to a "chemical mystery" more than a century old. "The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular." Soai, affiliated with the Tokyo University of Science, heard the news while he was shopping. He calls it one of the most beautiful days of his life. Million euros. The winners receive, besides eternal fame, an amount of just over one million euros in total, which they must share between the two of them. They may spend the money on whatever they like. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry last year went to a Japanese, a British and an American-Jordanian researcher. They researched so-called metal-organic frameworks. These are a kind of sponge that can slow the ripening of fruit and separate PFAS from water. Later this week the Nobel Prize for Literature and the Nobel Peace Prize will also be awarded. Next week the Nobel Prize for Economics follows, although that is actually not a real Nobel Prize, because it was not devised by Alfred Nobel himself. The Nobel Prize for Economics has only been awarded since 1969, the others since 1901.

title: Searches at livestock companies in Overijssel over possibly illegal cattle trade
lead: The <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> (NVWA) searched homes and business premises of two livestock traders from Overijssel last week. They are suspected of fraud in cattle trading, illegally collecting cattle and transporting animals that may not be transported. The suspicion is that the two livestock traders worked together, says a spokesperson for the NVWA. The traders may not have registered animals, or registered them incorrectly. This poses a risk to animal health. In the event of a problem with the meat, such as leftover medicine residues, it is difficult to trace where the meat comes from. The searches were carried out last week on Wednesday by the authority's Intelligence and Investigation Service (NVWA-IOD). Business administration, phones and ear tags for cattle were among the items seized. Also on that same day a livestock truck was intercepted that had left early in the morning from the premises of one of the traders. The truck held 21 cattle, none of which were registered at the trader's address. At another livestock farm in Overijssel a further 32 cattle belonging to the same suspect were found, which had been imported but not registered in the Netherlands. Unregistered cattle On the grounds of one of the traders were 88 animals that were not registered at that address, or not registered at all. At the other trader's it concerned 19 animals. There were also cattle without the mandatory ear tag, a metal or plastic plate with a unique number by which animals can be identified. The traders kept the real location of a business out of sight through incorrect registration. On paper the business was located at the address of the other trader. At the location that stayed out of sight were animals from domestic and foreign sources. Collecting animals for sale or slaughter may only take place at an approved location, the NVWA writes, and there are strict rules for that in order to prevent, for example, the spread of diseases. Sick animals The inspectors also found a barn with sick cows. Some could no longer stand, others had serious infections. The suspect is said to have transported these animals, although this is not allowed because of their poor health. The animals were examined urgently by the veterinarian; three cows had to be put out of their misery on the spot. The NVWA is ensuring that the other cows receive care. The suspects have not been arrested, but the criminal investigation is ongoing. Because of the investigation, the NVWA cannot say how it came to be on the trail of the two.

title: Stolen vase returns to Sicily: 'Farewell is painful, but serves a higher purpose'
lead: The Allard Pierson Archaeology Museum in Amsterdam has voluntarily returned an illegally excavated ancient vase to Sicily. The museum piece was handed over to an Italian delegation this morning. It is the Centuripe pyxis, which has been part of the collection for almost thirty years. The storage vessel from the third century BC depicts a wedding scene, watched over by the Greek god Apollo. "A unique piece. So richly decorated, polychrome and also with gold leaf", curator Laurien de Gelder describes the vase. "Saying goodbye always hurts a little", she admits, "but it serves a higher purpose." Missing papers The vase was bought in 1997 at the Tefaf fair in Maastricht from a Swiss dealer. Although provenance documentation and an export licence were missing, according to the seller that was not a problem. The vase was said to have been in Swiss private ownership since before 1970, the year in which a UNESCO convention laid down stricter rules. That it was otherwise became clear from a roll of film that Sicilian researchers came across in 2016. It contained not only family snapshots of the former village photographer from Centuripe, but the man also turned out to have documented the work and the loot of Sicilian grave robbers, including the pyxis. The roll of film also contained a wedding photo that turned out to date from 1976. The Swiss timeline proved to be a lie. "Things clearly did not go by the book", says Rogier Kalkers, who leads the provenance research into the Allard Pierson's collection. "When we received a restitution request, it made us think." Restitution is not legally required: our country only introduced the stricter rules in 2009, and they do not apply retroactively. "For forty years there has been a grey area for museums, collectors and dealers", says Kalkers. "Within it something may have been ethically reprehensible, but strictly speaking not legally punishable." The museum says it no longer sees that as an excuse to hide behind. "We want to take our responsibility and therefore also give it up." And so an Italian delegation came by today, including the island's heritage minister, carabinieri and a representative of the Italian embassy. Kalkers: "There is a lot of attention to this issue in traditional source countries such as Italy, Greece, Turkey and Egypt, but less in market countries such as the Netherlands." Cooperation Kalkers is not afraid of empty display cases. "That is the desired outcome for no one, not for Italy either." The museum could, for example, still have asked for a loan of the vase or for a replacement piece. Curator De Gelder: "Restitution is a solution to this kind of discussion, but it does not have to be the solution". Moreover, the return also gives the Allard Pierson something: ties with Sicily are being strengthened. The museum will carry out further research into such pottery together with Sicilian experts. That will yield more knowledge about its production and use, and facilitate detecting forgeries, De Gelder predicts. In the coming years the museum will also continue proactive provenance research into its own collection. "This is not a final step, but a stepping stone to joint follow-up research, in which we look with Sicilian and Italian authorities at how to proceed with other objects in our collection", says Kalkers. "We put less focus on ownership and more on shared custodianship."

title: Wild boars dig up cemetery in Schinnen: 'This is very painful'
lead: Wild boars have dug up the soil of several graves at a cemetery in Schinnen. The graves lie in a grass strip and there is a fence around them, but that does not keep the animals out. "It is very intense," says 88-year-old Nico Jetten to L1 Nieuws. One of the dug-up graves belongs to his late wife. She was buried last July in a new section of the cemetery. There are no traditional graves there, but small headstones on a grass patch. Three weeks ago Jetten wanted to visit his wife's grave when he came across the work of the wild boars. "It looked like a battlefield," he says. According to Jetten, the boars come to the cemetery at night. They do not dig as deep as the coffin, but he is afraid the headstones will be pushed over. "And it is simply painful." Warning signs hang at the cemetery: The cemetery is managed by the parish council. That council is aware of the problems, says grave manager Huub Scholz. A few years ago the cemetery was expanded and that area in particular is visited by the boars. "It is a green area with shrubs and trees, which the animals are drawn to." The cemetery is trying to put up a new fence as quickly as possible. The <entity id="org:gemeente-beekdaelen">gemeente Beekdaelen</entity> is involved and is working with the parish council on a solution. "A fence of about 150 meters will be installed at the back of the cemetery. Acoustic deterrents will also be temporarily used to keep the wild boars away," says a spokesperson.

title: Israel commemorates 7 October terror, gatherings also in the Netherlands
lead: In various places in Israel, commemorations of the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023 are being held today. Several ceremonies began this morning at 06.29 local time. At that time, three years ago today, the terrorist attacks began. In various cities and villages, people are coming together today to commemorate. Israeli media report that in some municipalities flags are flying at half-mast. This morning there was a nationwide minute of silence, and that also happened at 12.00 local time (11.00 Dutch time). At 18.29 local time, survivors and bereaved gather in Israel at the site where the Nova music festival took place three years ago. At that festival, 378 people were murdered and 44 people were abducted to the Gaza Strip. This is how Israelis commemorated the attacks in Kfar Aza, 5 kilometres from the border with Gaza: Later in the evening, the largest commemoration takes place at 21.15 local time in Yarkon Park in Tel Aviv. The commemoration is organised by Kumu, a national civic movement that was founded after the tragedy of 7 October. The organisation consists of survivors and relatives of victims and hostages. According to The Jerusalem Post, the group refused to take part in the official commemorations held by <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>. Many nationally organised commemorations already took place last Monday. The official national commemoration in Israel is legally fixed on the Hebrew date 24 Tishri, which falls on 5 October this year. The Hebrew calendar shifts every year relative to our calendar. What happened on 7 October 2023? Just after sunrise, the Palestinian terrorist organisation Hamas attacked Israel. It began with thousands of rockets fired at the country. Meanwhile, an estimated 6,000 Hamas militants crossed the border into Israel at dozens of points. Hamas members attacked military bases and stormed kibbutzim in small villages near the border. <entity id="org:gemeente-huizen">Huizen</entity> were set on fire and civilians were killed. The Nova music festival in the Negev desert was also a target. Festival-goers were shot en masse. 378 people were killed and 44 others were abducted. In total, about 1,200 people were killed in the attacks. 251 people were taken hostage. Of the hostages, 168 were ultimately released or rescued. The other 83 died. Israel responded to the attacks with a military offensive that resulted in genocidal violence. The war in Gaza has since already cost more than 74,000 Palestinians their lives. This morning there were also protests by anti-government demonstrators. They believe the government of Prime Minister Netanyahu failed in the run-up to 7 October and that independent investigation into the government's conduct must take place. In Tel Aviv, the fountain at Dizengoff Square was painted red. Photos and flowers have been laid on the fountain in memory of the victims. Demonstrators also blocked an important motorway in Tel Aviv for a moment of silence. They held up banners reading "The nation will not forget its sons and daughters". On a beach in Tel Aviv, unknown people placed an installation depicting 1,200 bodies. Next to it, the Hebrew text reads "total failure". There are also commemorations in the Netherlands. In <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, a gathering is being held at the Peace Palace, organised by the Council of Churches. It reports that Jews, Christians and Muslims will together commemorate the events and reflect on all civilian victims who fell on 7 October 2023 and later. Several speakers will take part in the commemoration. They will address the theme 'How do we move forward together?' Among others, pastor Birke Rapp, rabbi Marianne van Praag and imam Shamier Madhar will speak. In <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, the Israeli embassy and the Central Jewish Consultation are organising a commemoration. Batia Holin and her daughter Rotem Holin will talk about their personal experiences. They lived in the kibbutz Kfar Aza on 7 October 2023 and survived the attack by Hamas.

title: Hidden AI debts also a risk for Dutch investors
lead: Tech companies such as Meta are investing in special financial structures to keep AI investments off the balance sheet. Accountants must pay closer attention to this, says supervisor <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity>.

title: Schiedam shopping street floods after pipe burst
lead: A broken main water pipe has flooded a shopping street in the centre of Schiedam this morning. In some places the water stood 20 centimetres high. The financial damage runs into the hundreds of thousands. Works in the Hoogstraat hit the main water pipe, causing water to flow into the street. In some shops it also flowed inside. Water company Evides has shut off the main valve to prevent further damage. 'Everything is wet' "I came cycling up and suddenly I have a completely wet shop," says a shopkeeper to the regional broadcaster Rijnmond . "From the front all the way to the back of the warehouse." She runs a shop where people can sell things they have made themselves. "New, old and made items. Everything is now wet." Mopping is difficult, she says, because the water has nowhere to go. "The fire brigade is coming to help dry things up, with a sort of vacuum cleaner for water." At an architects' office further along, things stayed dry. "We immediately drew off water so that we can still make coffee," says an employee. "Now the water has been shut off." Not ready for move-in The works took place at nine new rental homes in the Hoogstraat. They were supposed to be ready for move-in by mid-November, but that is now delayed because four homes have water damage. "We have to open everything up," says contractor Julias Huis in 't Veld. "Plasterboard out, check the pipes. The insulation has to come out too, otherwise mould will form. It is a lot of extra work." The leak is also a financial setback, the contractor says. "The damage runs into the hundreds of thousands. Unfortunately people will have to wait even longer for their homes. And the worst part is that many businesses and shopkeepers here are suffering from it." Leak fixed Firefighters are helping to remove the water. For example, they are opening drains so it can flow away better. The exact location of the leak is not yet known, says Evides. The investigation into this may last until the end of the afternoon.

title: Podcast De Dag: the magic of Messi
lead: Lionel Messi has played for the last time in the blue and white of Argentina. Last night he said farewell as an international during a friendly match against Benin. With tears, fireworks and beautiful words, the footballer was honoured. Lionel Messi is the most decorated football player ever, with 47 football prizes. He has thus been named world's best footballer most often. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Don't forget to subscribe. But that did not go without a hitch, sports journalist Edwin Winkels tells us. He followed Messi closely in Barcelona and already heard early this century about a boy in the club's youth academy who was supposed to be very good. At FC Barcelona, Messi manages to climb and achieve great things. But his bond with Argentina's national team is more erratic. How did he become the football hero who has now been farewelled? Reactions? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editors: Max Smedes

title: Apeldoorn air disaster of 1946 commemorated again after ten years: 'Acknowledging grief'
lead: A plane crash in Apeldoorn from eighty years ago was commemorated again after ten years. The accident at the time killed 22 schoolchildren and the pilot. At today's commemoration, speeches were given and children laid wreaths at a monument. On 7 October 1946, a novice pilot flew a military aircraft over Apeldoorn. He had been chosen to fly to the Dutch East Indies, but first had to make a test flight. The plan was to do that near Valkenburg airfield, near Katwijk. But the pilot decided to fly to Apeldoorn, specifically to the then Christelijke HBS, now the Christelijke Lyceum. He wanted to impress his mother, who lived nearby. But it went wrong. The pilot hit the school's chimney with one wing, causing the fuel tank to come loose and fall through the roof of the gymnasium. At that moment 27 pupils were exercising in the hall. The aircraft's petrol caught fire and 22 pupils died. The pilot also did not survive the disaster. His mother rushed to the school after the accident. There she died of a heart attack when she heard her son had been killed. Boys died: the disaster made a huge impression on the residents of Apeldoorn. Dies Griffioen knows this all too well. The 80-year-old woman had just been born at the time of the disaster, but the incident also affected her family. "Everyone in Apeldoorn at some point heard that plane," she says. "It flew over the HBS three times before it crashed." Her grandmother was told that her son, Griffioen's uncle Willem van Kampen, had been seriously injured in the accident. He later died. Griffioen also thinks of the gym teacher, who struggled after the disaster. "He himself went into the school to look for children and his whole life he has felt that he should have died instead of all the boys." Silence: after the accident nothing more was said about it, Griffioen says. "The children were ordered to keep silent about the disaster. Among themselves they of course talked a little, but it was not allowed. It had to be kept quiet. After the war there was so much suffering that the strategy of the ggz was: silence." Forty years after the disaster the first commemoration was held. In 2016 that happened for the last time. Until now. "At first I thought: I don't want this anymore," says Dies Griffioen. "But then all that fear from the past creeps back. Like at home, where the accident was never processed. That means you constantly have a kind of enormous grief," she explains. "And it's as if a membrane is pulled off the wound. And then it all comes back up again." Griffioen today reflects on the boys who lost their lives, but also on the great grief of the bereaved. "It is also a kind of commemorating and acknowledging of the grief."

title: Several cars set on fire in parking garage in Zoetermeer, witnesses sought
lead: In a parking garage in Zoetermeer, several cars have recently been set on fire. The first fire was on 14 August, and last week fires followed on 30 September and 4 October. On the night of Monday to Tuesday, two cars were set on fire and an attempt was made to set a third on fire, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. Cars parked next to the burning cars also suffered damage. All the fires were at night. The police are investigating whether there is a connection between the arson attacks and are calling on witnesses to come forward. Camera surveillance: homes are located above the parking garage on Parkdreef. During the latest fire last night, residents had to leave their homes for some time. The municipality of Zoetermeer is introducing camera surveillance, the Zoetermeers Dagblad reports. The hope is that this will prevent new incidents. In addition, thanks to the surveillance, intervention can happen sooner.

title: Enough is enough for Hoogeveen after days of unrest: 'They want to fight with police'
lead:
In the centre of Hoogeveen, quiet this afternoon, a terrace visitor curiously points at a group of teenagers hanging around a monument. "Are those the kids sitting there?" he asks a restaurant employee. "Yes," the employee explains. "But they can go far, mind you." During the day Kerkplein by Hoofdstraat is still peaceful, but in recent evenings fireworks, eggs and stones flew through the air. Passersby and business owners are being intimidated by a group of young people aged between 10 and 17. That is why the municipality is stepping in. Mayor <entity id="person:martijn-breukelman">Martijn Breukelman</entity> is declaring a security risk area from today, after evenings of unrest, so that people can be searched preventively. The cameras set up a few days ago did not yet have the desired effect. Neither did the ban on gatherings. The source of the unrest is not entirely clear to the municipality. Boredom is said to play a role. "But it concerns behaviour we absolutely do not accept," stresses Mayor Breukelman. That is why, for the municipality, enough is enough: "The time for consultation is over, we are now taking firm action."

Unsafe

For residents and business owners the situation has become unbearable. Erwin Slomp, chairman of Stichting Binnenstad Hoogeveen, sees how the shopping climate is suffering from the unrest. "People no longer feel safe when cobras or other fireworks are thrown at them. Shopkeepers and their staff are being intimidated, and visitors no longer dare to go into Hoofdstraat. This is a line that has been crossed." In recent evenings several young people were pulled off their fatbikes by police, arrested or fined. During searches the police came across not only fireworks but also stabbing weapons and brass knuckles. Almost all of them are minors, so the police are also talking to the parents.

'Dead village'

According to the young people in the centre this afternoon, the troublemakers are mainly motivated by a combination of boredom, peer pressure and a thirst for sensation. "People just want to act tough and show that they're mafia," says a 15-year-old boy on a fatbike. "They just want to fight with the police." A blond boy of just 13 says that the boys who cause nuisance in the evenings know each other from Hoogeveen. They come from different schools. In online groups they rally each other to come along too. "Finally something is happening in this dead village. When everyone's there, it's fun. Right now it's mostly about challenging the police with fireworks and then riding away as fast as possible." He understands that the situation is getting out of hand: "My parents think it's awful. I'm still allowed to meet up in the evenings, but actually not come into the centre anymore." A question whether he will listen to his parents is answered only with a smile.

Appeal to parents

Together with the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the municipality is mapping the identities of the nuisance-causers. So far more than 65 names are known. All of their parents can expect a letter. Both the mayor and the city centre association point emphatically to the role of parents. Breukelman: "14- or 15-year-olds with knives or boxing knuckles, that's no longer mischief." Slomp also makes an urgent appeal to parents: "Know where your child is in the evenings and what they are doing. There is also a personal responsibility there."

title: Suspect in Herkenbosch murder now also suspected of murdering his own mother
lead: Daniel B., the German man suspected of the murder of Paul Vossen from Herkenbosch in Limburg, is now also suspected of murdering his mother. The prosecution service announced this afternoon at the court in <entity id="org:gemeente-roermond">Roermond</entity>. The woman has already been missing for almost two years. The police and prosecutors already had "strong indications" that B. had something to do with his mother's disappearance, but not enough for a formal suspicion of murder. That is now different. The Public Prosecution Service has not disclosed what new evidence or leads there are. The 48-year-old B. was questioned last month about his mother's disappearance. In a storage unit in the German municipality of Heinsberg, items with the woman's blood were previously found. In another storage unit, which was in her name, there were shovels and a rake. The woman did not have a garden herself. The police suspect the items were used to bury the woman. B. denies all involvement in her disappearance. He also says he has nothing to do with the death of Paul Vossen. Home invasion: Daniel B. was arrested in September last year on suspicion of murdering Vossen, earlier that month. The OM thinks the man was killed during a failed home invasion. Vossen (66) had just retired and was found with serious injuries in the garden of his villa in Herkenbosch. He died shortly afterwards. B. was not far from Herkenbosch at the time. The apartment in Montfort where he was arrested was in the name of his mother Teresa Krug. The woman, of Polish origin, had not been seen since March 2025 but was never reported missing. Searches for her body have so far yielded nothing. The two cases are being handled simultaneously, L1 Nieuws reports. That will probably happen next year.

title: Ten injured in stabbing at school in Poland, suspect (19) arrested
lead: Ten people were injured in a stabbing at a vocational school in northern Poland. A 19-year-old student from the school was arrested in the area. The injured are five pupils, two teachers, two bystanders and the perpetrator. The latter injured himself, local authorities report. No one is in life-threatening danger. However, one person sustained serious injuries and a number of victims were transported by helicopter to a hospital. The attack with a "sharp object" took place around 11.00 in Ostroleka, about 120 kilometers northeast of Warsaw. The authorities have not disclosed a possible motive. The police shared a photo of the arrest: the suspect was apprehended less than a kilometer from the school, after he had fled. He was taken to hospital with unknown injuries. Two hours after the attack, the mayor of Ostroleka announced that the school will remain closed so the authorities can investigate the scene of the attack.

title: Extensive mortgage fraud by criminals, report has been sitting in a drawer for months
lead: Over the past few years, between 6000 and 11.000 homes in the Netherlands have been bought with forged papers. By committing fraud when applying for a mortgage, criminals manage to gain possession of the houses in order to carry out illegal activities there. That is what an unpublished report says, which according to insiders has been sitting at the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> for over six months. The report was drawn up by the Financieel Expertise Centrum, which received an assignment from the previous <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> to research the "aard en omvang" of mortgage fraud in the Netherlands. Members of parliament, but also the Dutch Association of Banks (NVB) and the professional association of <entity id="org:zbo-notarissen">notarissen</entity> have been very worried about this form of fraud for several years. Criminals manage to buy properties with the help of, for example, forged payslips, employer statements, annual financial statements or tax returns. Undermining The purchased homes are being used for "money laundering, illegal rental, labour exploitation, drug crime and other forms of undermining", said NVB chair Medy van der Laan today in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. She was there for a hearing on undermining crime. The outcome of the report, which was due to be ready in March, has been awaited for months. "Mortgage fraud is increasingly taking place", said Van der Laan. "Exploitation takes place, fraud and many other terrible things. And it disrupts the liveability of a neighbourhood." In 2024, reports came out via the Financieele Dagblad about a criminal network that bought hundreds of homes in the Amsterdam region between 2018 and 2023 through fraud. Those properties turned out to have been used for, among other things, storing money and drugs, and migrant workers were housed there. The fraudsters, mostly Bulgarian migrant workers, had been hired by administrative offices to forge payslips. In the Tweede Kamer, VVD and NSC, among others, asked the then cabinet questions about it. Pro has also been pressing for measures for some time. The Royal Notarial Professional Organisation of notaries (KNB) also points to "deficient legislation" and "limited possibilities for information exchange". Checking with the tax authorities Just like banks, notaries would like the option to verify income details with the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>. That should not be a problem. "We respect all sensitivities around privacy. When an application comes in, we only want to check whether the data we have received is correct", said Van der Laan. Pro MP Mutluer urges that the report and the recommendations be sent to the House as soon as possible. A debate on this subject is also scheduled for next week.

title: 200,000 Yemenis flee as fighting flares up
lead: The UN organisation for migration and refugee aid (IOM) is sounding the alarm over the situation in Yemen. Since fighting between the Houthis and the government army flared up again at the beginning of last month , around 200,000 Yemenis have fled. "People are running for their lives but find no safety anywhere," says IOM director Amy Pope. "They now need shelter, food and safety. Our people are on the ground, but the funding is not." Pope calls on donor countries to act. "Yemen must not become a forgotten crisis. The world has the means to help. Those must now be used." More than thirteen years For many refugees, this is not the first time they have had to leave their homes. The civil war in Yemen has been going on for more than thirteen years. It began with an uprising by the Iran-backed Houthis. The government army has the support of Saudi Arabia. Through UN mediation, a ceasefire came into effect in 2022. That was broken last month by an offensive by the Houthis. They gained control of the entire area along the Red Sea. From there, missiles and drones are being used to attack airfields, military complexes and oil installations in Saudi Arabia, again today. The conquests increase the Houthis' ability to attack shipping traffic in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the link between the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government army have launched a counteroffensive to push back the Houthis. The fighting is currently mainly taking place near the town of Dhubab on the Red Sea and in the area south of the city of Ta'izz. These are images from Monday of the government army's offensive at the Bab el-Mandeb Strait:

title: House of Representatives backs alcohol meter for convicted offenders
lead: A majority in the House of Representatives supports introducing the alcohol meter. This is an ankle band for people who have been convicted of a crime involving alcohol and who have received an alcohol ban from the judge. It may concern, for example, a traffic accident or domestic violence. The alcohol meter absorbs skin moisture and sweat and detects whether there is alcohol in it. The probation service receives a notification when alcohol is consumed and contacts this person. If it has been established that the person indeed drank, and that it was not, for example, cleaning product that someone was working with, then a warning follows. Pilots The law was already prepared by previous cabinets but only now comes before the House. The alcohol meter was tested in pilots in which convicted persons could voluntarily choose the ankle band instead of urine and blood tests. In 2023, nearly 1500 people were given an alcohol ban or an alcohol and drug ban. Of the people with an alcohol meter, 10 percent committed an offence while wearing the ankle band, compared with 51 percent of persons with only urine checks. These more positive effects were also present three months after the ankle band was removed, according to police figures. Do not refuse Refusing to wear the alcohol meter while the judge has imposed an alcohol ban is seen as refusing a sentence. This also applies to attempts to remove the ankle band. Alcohol meters cost around 1500 euros. In case of damage or loss, the wearer must pay the costs. Unlike an ankle band, an alcohol meter cannot trace where someone is.

title: 'Drifting' motorcyclist sentenced to community service for fatal accident in Lelystad
lead: A motorcyclist who caused a fatal accident in Lelystad two years ago has been sentenced to 240 hours of community service. The 32-year-old man must also pay compensation of 37,000 euros to the parents of the victim. The accident happened on 2 June 2024 on the Karperweg in Lelystad during an illegal 'drift' event. Hundreds of spectators were present. When drifting on a motorcycle, the rider deliberately loses grip on the rear wheel, which slides sideways through the bend. The motorcyclist from Schiedam ended up on the wrong side of the road and collided head-on with a dirt bike. The 18-year-old rider of that bike, from Maarssen, died two days later from his injuries, reports Omroep Flevoland. Motorcycles gone The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded eight months' imprisonment. The court imposed a much lower sentence, partly because the man from Schiedam had no criminal record and expressed remorse. After the fatal accident, the man got rid of his motorcycles and says he never wants to ride a motorcycle again. According to the judge, the man was careless and inattentive, but not reckless. The court writes in the verdict that the suspect, although the outcome was fatal, actually broke one traffic rule: failing to keep sufficiently to the right. According to the OM, there was an illegal street race, but the judge does not agree. Participants did drift, but according to the court it was not about speed. A 36-year-old man from Rotterdam who, according to the OM, organized the drift event has been acquitted of manslaughter. According to the court, he did not organize an illegal street race, and it cannot be established with certainty that he gave the start signal for the drift with fatal consequences.

title: Couple in US charged for abuse in 'horror house' full of surrogate children
lead: A couple from California has been charged in a case involving the abuse of at least fifteen children aged between two months and thirteen years old. Fourteen of the children were reportedly born through surrogacy. According to the prosecutors, the children were beaten and punched by nannies in the couple's villa. Guojun Xuan (66) and Silvia Zhang (39) kept most of the children in their villa in Arcadia, about 20 kilometers from Los Angeles. The children were housed in their home and cared for by nannies, the prosecutors stated. They reportedly spent hours a day in three different rooms of the villa, so-called 'learning centers', where the nannies supervised. Thirty-two surveillance cameras were found in the villa last year. According to justice officials, the couple thus kept an eye on the nannies. Footage recorded how they systematically hit the children and punished them harshly. The couple is accused of recruiting women to become surrogate mothers and of conspiring to have the children abused. Public prosecutor Nathan Hochman called the villa a "horror house". "The number of children exposed to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented", he said. The couple was arrested yesterday and says it is innocent. According to American media, they wanted to create a large family. Head injury The investigation began after a two-month-old baby with a head injury was brought to the hospital in July last year. One of the nannies reportedly struck the newborn on the head. Hospital staff did not trust it and alerted the police. An arrest warrant was issued for the nanny last year, but she is reportedly still on the run. Twenty-one children under the couple's supervision were placed elsewhere: fifteen were removed from the villa and six were elsewhere. Most of the children were between one and three years old. The couple was already detained at that time, because they reportedly knew their baby was injured and did not raise the alarm. The couple was released on bail because no formal charges had yet been filed. Now that the Public Prosecution Service and police have concluded the investigation, the pair could be arrested again. Surrogate mothers Besides the abuse, the couple is also suspected of making false statements to at least two women who became surrogate mothers. Zhang reportedly said she had difficulty getting pregnant. The prosecutors expect that the surrogate mothers came from different parts of the United States and did not know that others were also carrying embryos for the pair.

title: Police in Bavaria searching for a puma or something resembling one
lead: A municipality close to Munich airport in the German state of Bavaria is calling on residents to be careful because a wild, cat-like animal has been spotted. It may be a puma. Police have launched a large search operation. A helicopter and drones have been deployed. The animal was spotted last night by a hunter using a night-vision scope. That was in the Notzinger Moos nature reserve, a few kilometres from the airport. He made a video of it. Experts viewed the footage overnight and concluded it is possibly a puma. No panic. The municipality of Erding, which issued the warning, does not want to cause panic. "We want to make sure people keep a slightly better eye on their surroundings," a spokesperson tells regional broadcaster BR . Anyone who sees the animal or knows where it is hiding should not go there but call the police immediately. Dog owners are advised to keep their dogs on a lead. "And do not let your small children play outside unsupervised," the spokesperson said. Puma and lion. It would not be the first time that an animal in Germany has been mistaken for a puma or lion. Last year a search for a puma was also launched in the state of Saxony-Anhalt. It was not found. According to an expert, it must have been a cat. In 2023 police in Berlin searched for 30 hours for a lion that had supposedly escaped. It was not found either. It was probably a wild boar.

title: Swastikas daubed in many places in Nieuw-Lekkerland on Israeli flag
lead: Swastika graffiti has been found in dozens of places in Nieuw-Lekkerland in the <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">provincie Zuid-Holland</entity>. The municipality is filing a report. The Reformatorisch Dagblad had already reported earlier on the graffiti. In images shared by the newspaper, paving stones can be seen on which Israeli flags have been sprayed with a spray can. In the places where the Star of David should be, there is a swastika. The graffiti is being removed. A number of tiles may need to be replaced. Mayor <entity id="person:theo-segers">Theo Segers</entity> of the <entity id="org:gemeente-molenlanden">gemeente Molenlanden</entity>, to which Nieuw-Lekkerland belongs, calls the graffiti "very objectionable" to news agency ANP. Not the first time The swastikas were, according to the municipality, applied overnight. A spokesperson reports that graffiti has meanwhile been removed in about thirty locations. "They may be found in even more places." The municipality expects everything to be cleaned up tomorrow. It is not the first time swastikas have been applied in the public space of Nieuw-Lekkerland. That also happened earlier this year. At that time street furniture and bus shelters were defaced because of the possible arrival of an asylum seekers' centre. A resident of the village then decided to stick stickers with hearts on the swastikas: It is exactly three years today since the terrorist organisation Hamas carried out a major attack on Israel. More than 1200 people died and 251 people were taken hostage. Today the Hamas attacks are commemorated in many places around the world, including in the Netherlands, among others in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>.

title: Mayor of Oldebroek attends Coming Out Day celebration after college scraps LGBTI policy
lead: Oldebroek is raising the rainbow flag on Coming Out Day, but not at the town hall. The Christian-conservative college of the Veluwe municipality officially decided last week to stop its LGBTI policy and no longer raise the rainbow flag. This was already in the coalition agreement of the Christelijk Verbond Oldebroek (CVO), the SGP and Algemeen Belang Oldebroek (ABO). At the Kruiskerk the rainbow flag will fly on Saturday. And mayor <entity id="person:tanja-haseloop-amsing">Tanja Haseloop-Amsing</entity> will be present when the flag is raised, although the college decided to continue "without woke expressions". Haseloop-Amsing (VVD) tells Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> that she is not only chair of the college of B and W, but that she has her own role and her own line. "As mayor I am also an independent administrative body, which must keep an eye on whether we in this village still get along reasonably well with each other. That there is administrative integrity. That role as village mother I am now taking on." Flag action. Reverend Han Wilmink of the Kruiskerk will raise the flag, as every year. He finds that this year it is especially important. "This municipal policy gives people a signal: you don't belong. We have to push back against that and resist it." State secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity>, who comes from the region, will also be present, writes Trouw . After the presentation of the coalition agreement in July, resident Kjeld Mooi decided to stand up against the municipal government's plans to scrap LGBTI policy. At the installation of the college he stood in front of the town hall with a rainbow flag. He received much support for his action, including from LGBTI people in the municipality who said they always have to keep their sexual orientation hidden. Coming Out Day is on Sunday 11 October, but the organisation in Oldebroek is holding the gathering on Saturday already, out of respect for the Sunday rest. Anyone in the village who wants one can get a rainbow flag to hang outside at home on Saturday. More than 250 flags have already been requested.

title: Temporary protection or asylum? Ukrainians are unsure where they stand
lead: Mixed feelings among Ukrainians after it became known that their asylum applications must be assessed. "On the one hand there is a faint hope that an end will come to the temporary nature of our stay, but on the other hand we still don't know where we stand", says Ukrainian Jamal Statsenko. Anna Bieliaieva of Vital'nya, a community for Ukrainian refugees in the Netherlands, shares this experience. "We hear more and more that people are aware of the European ruling, but what will happen now remains unclear." Last week, the European Court of Justice ruled that the Netherlands must start assessing asylum applications from over 140,000 Ukrainians. A problem for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, because the asylum system will come under even more pressure as a result. 'Must we go back, or do we stay here?' For Ukrainians who fled their country after the war broke out, the Temporary Protection Directive was activated for the first time. This is a European rule designed to quickly offer temporary protection in a situation of a large influx of refugees. As a result, Ukrainians immediately gained the right to shelter, work, medical care and education for their children. "Since the start of the war, they have actually been in a very pleasant waiting room. But even if you are in a waiting room that is very comfortable, it is still a waiting room", says Mark Klaassen, university lecturer in immigration law at the University of <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>. Europe keeps extending the protection, now until March 2028. But the question remains what will happen after that. According to Ukrainians, that uncertainty is the big problem. "My son has lived here for half his life. He speaks Dutch and has his social life here with friends", says Bieliaieva. "Lately he keeps asking which school he will go to after group 8. Must we go back, or are we still here? I can't give an answer to that." Flood of asylum applications The advantage of that special European rule is that an individual asylum procedure does not have to be followed. Immigration services therefore do not suddenly have an enormous number of applications to process. The Netherlands has got it wrong. Here the rule was implemented in such a way that Ukrainians had to submit an asylum application, after which they received that temporary European protection. The asylum applications were then put on hold until the temporary protection expires. That is not allowed, the European Court now says: the asylum applications are separate from the temporary protection. Since the Netherlands had the Ukrainians submit such an application, those must also be assessed. A headache of a file for the ministry. "Let alone for the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity>, which is currently dealing with a backlog of over 50,000 people waiting for a decision. On top of that, they are facing this flood of cases", says Klaassen. Ukrainians are currently not building up residence rights. "With asylum status you build up years of residence; in theory you could become Dutch after five years. Those years do not count for Ukrainians at the moment", says the university lecturer in immigration law. Uncertainty remains It will still be a while before Ukrainians hear anything about their asylum application. Asylum minister Van den Brink wants to first process the people who are arriving now, then clear the waiting list, and after that it will be the turn of the Ukrainian group. However, in a letter to parliament today, he emphasises that the European ruling has no effect on the way municipalities currently organise the reception of Ukrainians. According to Statsenko, an asylum status would help him get his own home. "With temporary protection, the chance of getting a mortgage is very small. It is also much harder to rent; landlords have trouble with that temporariness." Not all Ukrainians are waiting for such an asylum procedure, says Bieliaieva. "Of course there are people who want to go back. We love Ukraine, and of course we would have preferred never to have left." Until the ministry has worked out how it will concretely address this situation, it remains a matter of waiting. "I hope to finally get clarity for the future and not another temporary extension", says Statsenko. Bieliaieva also wants the opportunity to build something here for real. "It would be nice if we knew where we stand. But at heart, not much changes. We don't know exactly what this means."

title: Pro-Palestinian protest with Hamas support statements in Amsterdam dispersed
lead: A pro-Palestinian protest on the Dam in Amsterdam has been dispersed by <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity>. During the gathering, slogans such as 'long live the 7th of October' were chanted, referring to the Hamas attacks in Israel on 7 October 2023. Demonstrators also burned an Israeli flag. Protesters wearing face masks held up a large green banner reading 'we support Hamas'. Men with scarves over their faces held a banner reading 'glory to our martyrs, victory to the resistance'. Law not broken The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has looked at the statements on the Dam and judged that the texts on the banners do not break the law. Asked whether such texts are not tasteless on the day the massacre that Hamas carried out in Israel three years ago is commemorated, an organiser responded: "Tasteless? I don't know. It is provocative and I understand why people do it." The man is angry about a law being drafted to make glorification of terrorism punishable. According to the man, the Netherlands should not see Hamas as a terrorist organisation but as a political movement, and support for it should not be punishable. Demonstrators who continued into the city from the Dam wanted to go to the neighbourhood with many Jewish buildings. The police prevented the group from going that way, after which the group continued protesting in front of the Stopera, the town hall. There an Israeli flag was set on fire. Demonstration dispersed An estimated 150 demonstrators were present on the Dam, and about half of them then continued into the city. At 20.15 hours the demonstration was dispersed on the mayor's orders, because some demonstrators did not follow the instruction to go to the Stopera. The protesters then left the area. Mayor Halsema calls the statements of support by the demonstrators at the National Monument on the Dam "shocking and tasteless", but also says that they are not punishable and that intervening on the Dam was therefore not possible.

title: Six arrests for the theft of Renoir paintings in southern France
lead: A month after the painting theft from the Renoir museum in southern France, French police have arrested six suspects. Among them are the two alleged burglars, French media report. The arrests were made in four different departments in the south and east of France. The six are suspected, among other things, of organised theft. They have been taken to Nice for questioning. On 8 September, four paintings by the well-known French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir were stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer. During their escape, the two thieves left two paintings behind in the museum garden. Most valuable paintings It is not yet clear whether the other two have been recovered. The works are Madame Colonna Romano and Jeune Femme au puits (Young Woman at the Well). The paintings were on loan from the Musée d'Orsay in Paris. The thieves appeared well prepared. They entered through a glass door at around 06.00 in the morning and removed the canvases in less than 3 minutes. These were the four most valuable pieces in the museum. It opened in 1960 in Renoir's last home. When police arrived there, it turned out that part of the fence had been cut, allowing the perpetrators onto the grounds. Security footage later showed that the thieves had sawn through the anchoring of the paintings in the wall.

title: Figurehead of Spanish housing protests Maricarmen Abascal (87) has died
lead: Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman who became the face and namesake of the housing protests in Spain, has died. The Spanish tenants' union announced this. Abascal was evicted from her home, where she had lived for seventy years. Due to a rent increase she could no longer afford her home. Her eviction was the direct reason for the protests in Spain. Many Spaniards cannot pay for housing due to inflation and a shortage of homes. Especially in the cities Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia there is too little housing. The country also has a major shortage of social rental housing. This concerns less than 2 percent of the available supply, while the European average is 8 percent. Maricarmen quickly became the face of the housing crisis in Spain: hundreds of demonstrators were present at Abascal's eviction. They regarded it as a new low point in the country's housing crisis. The activists tried to prevent the eviction, but police dispersed them with tear gas. Eventually the eviction was reversed and the woman could remain living in her home. Decrees adopted: Yesterday the Spanish government approved two housing market decrees. The measures for rent ceilings, a temporary ban on evictions and restrictions on the purchase of homes by companies were, according to Prime Minister Sánchez, 'based on pure common sense'. He stated that opinion polls showed that a large majority of the population supports intervention in the housing market. The same decrees were rejected by parliament last week. Sánchez then called early elections for 29 November. Due to the dissolution of parliament, the measures can now be temporarily introduced and subsequently be submitted to a smaller permanent body of 69 parliamentarians that remains in place during the election period. There is sufficient support to keep the measures in place. The decrees have also been named after Maricarmen Abascal. Prime Minister Sánchez has expressed his condolences to the bereaved following her death.

title: Climate change cause of rapid decline of chinstrap penguin on British island
lead: British scientists have established that the population of chinstrap penguins on a British island in the southern Atlantic Ocean has declined dramatically. In 2011, Zavodovski Island had 900,000 chinstrap penguins and 90,000 macaroni penguins. Fourteen years later, the number of chinstrap penguins had fallen by 63 percent, while the number of macaroni penguins had actually increased. The scientists of the British Antarctic Survey (BAS) attribute the "alarming" decline of the first group to climate change. The diet of chinstrap penguins consists mainly of krill: small shrimp-like creatures. "As the water warmed, the krill moved south," says BAS scientist Norman Ratcliffe to the BBC. "Because of the sea ice in the south and the lack of suitable islands to nest on, the chinstrap penguins cannot follow their food." That the macaroni penguins are doing well is probably because they have a more varied diet; those animals also eat fish and crustaceans. Other explanations The researchers also looked at other possible explanations for the decline of the chinstrap penguin, such as the volcanic eruption on Zavodovski Island in 2016 and competition from other krill predators, such as macaroni penguins, whales and fishing. These alternative explanations proved untenable. Chinstrap penguins also occur on other islands in the Antarctic region. Scientists are seeing numbers decline there too. The BAS scientists think chinstrap penguins will be listed as endangered species if the trend continues. Their research can be found in Current Biology.

title: WWF: wild animal populations declined considerably since 1970, 'but nature recovery is possible'
lead: Populations of birds, mammals, reptiles and other vertebrates have declined by nearly three quarters on average since 1970, according to a biennial report from the World Wide Fund for Nature. There are, however, large differences: half of the populations studied are stable or increasing. The other half is declining, sometimes sharply. A population is a group of animals of the same species that live close together. Think of a group of savanna elephants in Zambia or a group of otters in the Weerribben in Overijssel. Most animal species consist of several populations that have limited contact with one another. A population can consist of a handful of animals, but also of thousands of individuals. "The most important message of this report is that nature recovery is within reach," says Robert Zwiers, head of impact at WWF. "Wild animals are under serious pressure worldwide, but we also see that wild animals are making a comeback worldwide." Otters and sharks Examples of success stories are the tiger, the green sea turtle, the bluefin tuna and the otter in the Netherlands, says Zwiers. "Otters had become extinct in the Netherlands. Thanks to cleaner water, connecting habitats and reintroducing otters, they are doing well here again. The bluefin tuna is no longer threatened by catch quotas." Sharks and rays, on the other hand, are declining sharply, says Zwiers. "Many species grow slowly and have few offspring, which makes them vulnerable. They are caught and also regularly end up as bycatch in fishing nets. Existing agreements are not enough to protect these species." 5,790 species The World Wide Fund for Nature bases its conclusions on data from 5,790 different species of mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles and fish. For this it looked at 35,803 populations around the world. Species such as insects, jellyfish and crabs were therefore not included in the study. For each population, the researchers determined the trend since 1970: did the population increase, decrease, or remain stable? Half of the populations declined, 7 percent of the populations remained stable and the remaining 43 percent of the populations actually grew. Even so, the average is negative, with a decline of 73 percent. According to Zwiers, this is because the declining populations decline more sharply than the growing populations grow. Repeat of research The figures are not surprising. The previous edition of the Living Planet Report from 2024 also found that the average size of monitored wild animal populations worldwide fell by 73 percent since 1970. "You cannot compare these figures one-to-one because we have now used more data, but this research confirms the earlier picture," says Zwiers. To restore populations that are in a tight spot, he says it is necessary, among other things, to produce our food more sustainably, accelerate the energy transition and phase out investments in the financial sector that harm nature.

title: European Court of Auditors warns of rapidly rising EU debt burden
lead: The European Court of Auditors (ERK) is concerned about the growing debt burden of the European Union. That debt has risen in recent years to 740 billion euros. In 2027 the EU debt will likely grow further to 1 trillion (1,000,000,000,000) euros. The rise in debt is mainly due to support for Ukraine, rising interest rates, defence spending and the COVID-19 Recovery Fund. That fund was created in 2020 to support the economy during the economic crisis caused by the coronavirus pandemic. Still more than 112 billion euros in recovery payments must be paid out from the COVID-19 Recovery Fund. Brussels wants to shape part of the EU multiannual budget (2028-2034) in the same way as the COVID-19 Recovery Fund. That means costs are not reimbursed afterwards, but countries receive money in advance when they submit their plans. In those plans they must make clear how they intend to achieve EU targets. The Court says in its annual report that a multiannual budget based on the COVID-19 Recovery Fund carries risks. EU countries were allowed to loosen or limit plans in the COVID-19 Recovery Fund without convincing reasons and evidence. This created the risk that countries received EU money for delivering fewer results than had been promised in advance. The Court considers this system of submitting plans in advance 'too vague' and 'not verifiable'. For example, the Court found irregularities of 45.5 billion euros in the EU accounts for 2025. These involved, among other things, persistent problems with control systems in member states.

title: Software pioneer of the first moon landing Margaret Hamilton (90) has died
lead: Margaret Hamilton, who developed the software for the first moon landing of Apollo 11 in 1969, has died. Thanks to her groundbreaking work in the field of software development, the Americans were able to fly to the moon with Apollo and land there. With this landing the Americans won the space race in the 1960s. Hamilton died on 30 September at the age of 90. Her death was announced by MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), the institute where she worked for many years. Hamilton joined MIT in 1959 and continued working there until the mid-1970s. Initially she developed software to make weather forecasting better. At that time computer science was not an official subject and programmers learned the work in practice. Hamilton also taught herself programming. Later Hamilton ended up in the research group working on the software for the Apollo program. In 1961 this department won a contract with NASA. Eventually she led a team of one hundred engineers who designed the software for controlling NASA's Apollo missions. Hamilton is regarded as one of the founders of the field of software engineering, a term she herself coined. Professor Oliver Weck of the MIT Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics says of Hamilton: "To say that she was a pioneer and that she was far ahead of her time would be a huge understatement. She was a software engineer at a time when this field was still in its infancy; she not only developed advanced code herself, but also led a team that used this emerging technology to develop one of the most complex systems humankind has ever produced." In 2016 Hamilton was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Barack Obama for her contribution to science and spaceflight. In 2017 Margaret Hamilton described her experiences during the Apollo project in an interview:

title: Wake-up call 8/10: Nobel Prize for Literature announced • Who wins a Televizier-Ring?
lead: Good morning! Today the Nobel Committee announces who wins the Nobel Prize for Literature, and in Carré the Gold Televizier-Ring will be presented. First the weather: today sunny spells, clouds and a few showers alternate. With moderate to strong north-westerly wind it will be 14 to 16 degrees. Tomorrow there is a strong wind, it is cloudy and there is rain for a considerable time. The weekend is changeable with sun, clouds and showers at around 14 degrees. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman who became the face of the housing protests in Spain, has died. The Spanish tenants' union announced this. Abascal was evicted from her home, where she had lived for seventy years. Because of a rent increase she could no longer afford her home. Her eviction was the direct trigger for the protests in Spain. Other news from the night: And one more thing: In Tel Aviv, the 1,200 Israelis killed were commemorated yesterday, who died three years ago in the Hamas attack of 7 October. There were also ceremonies at other places in Israel, some of which started at 06.29 local time. At that time Hamas began the terrorist attacks in 2023. Have a nice day!

title: Report: deliberately created crisis makes recovery impossible for Gazans
lead: Three years after the start of the devastating war in Gaza, Palestinians are trapped in a cycle of displacement and violence, with hardly any access to food, clean drinking water or care, says Dokters van de Wereld. The overall health of the Palestinian population is steadily deteriorating, with irreversible damage as a result.
