For example, that a certain percentage must consist of recycled material. "Then a market will develop for it and it will become economically viable." Trade associations of furniture manufacturers CBM and RND support the introduction of producer responsibility. However, CBM says it must happen in a "workable way", and RND says data must first be available on how much furniture can be recycled and reused "in a profitable way" before targets are set. The municipalities hope for cooperation with the manufacturers. "Furniture producers take back as much old furniture as possible themselves when they sell new furniture. For the remaining part, municipalities are happy to help collect it," says NVRD director Eijer. The municipalities also expect to continue playing a role in recycling. "It will be quite difficult for companies to do that in a good way."

title: Criticism of execution via livestream, Trump says decision not yet final
lead: US President Trump says it has not yet been definitively decided to livestream the execution of a US soldier. Much criticism followed the announcement of this by Minister Hegseth yesterday. "Well, they still have to make a decision about it," Trump said evasively without going into detail when asked about the planned execution. "But he will be killed, that will be done by a firing squad." Trump added that it "really doesn't matter how he goes, as long as he goes. I think the death penalty is a dignified way for him to go." 'Disgusting' On Thursday Minister Hegseth announced that the execution of Nidal Hasan "will be open for everyone to follow". The Pentagon later explained that it is considering a livestream. Former major Hasan shot thirteen colleagues dead at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009. The Palestinian-American soldier stated that he did this to protect Muslims in Afghanistan. If the execution is indeed livestreamed, it will be the first public execution in the US since 1936. It is also the first time since 1961 that the US army carries out a death sentence. American politicians react shocked to the idea, including Republican party colleagues of Trump. The influential senator Thom Tillis calls it "more than disgusting" and says that by doing this the US is joining the list of "tyrannical dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan". His colleague John Curtis warns that the Roman statesman and thinker Seneca already warned about bloody spectacles in Rome: "A civilisation declines when it regards executions as a form of entertainment". 'Sick' Democratic senators are even harsher. Jon Ossoff calls it an "obscene medieval spectacle" and finds Hegseth "a sick person who seems to revel in this kind of cruelty". His party colleague Jack Reed speaks of "a gift to anti-American terrorism recruiters". Vice President JD Vance also reacts unenthusiastically. "I don't know whether it will really happen," he told reporters briefly. Afterwards he preferred to talk mainly about Hasan's crimes: "The method may be controversial, but I hope people do not forget that this man cruelly murdered many innocent people". He added on his own that he would not watch the livestream himself. "I won't watch it."

title: Pedestrian killed on the A58 near Tilburg
lead: Someone died overnight on the A58 near Tilburg. The victim presumably wanted to cross the motorway, Omroep Brabant reports. A lorry could not avoid the pedestrian. Many emergency services were called out, including a trauma helicopter. The victim turned out to have already died. The A58 was closed near Tilburg for some time after the accident. Why the pedestrian was on the motorway is still being investigated. Nothing has yet been made public about the identity of the person.

title: Arson at the railway, no trains between Rotterdam and Delft
lead: A fire was set at a railway bridge at Rotterdam-Delfshaven last night. This has major consequences for train traffic; it is at least at a standstill for the rest of the day between the Rotterdam Centraal and Delft Campus stations. Around 02:30 a fault occurred at the railway bridge. A contractor who went to investigate the fault saw that the door of a technical room had been ground open. Smouldering cables were inside. According to a spokesperson for rail infrastructure manager ProRail, a fire was set there. Sabotage is possible. The fire brigade has been present at the railway bridge over the Delfshavense Schie since last night. The fire has been put out and the technical room is being ventilated so that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> can carry out its investigation. Once the police have finished the investigation, ProRail can only go inside to assess the damage and draw up a recovery plan. How large the damage is will therefore only become clear later. No trains It is certain that no trains will run between Rotterdam and Delft all day today. "I do not rule out that it could take longer", says a ProRail spokesperson. The track between Rotterdam and Delft is one of the busiest in the Netherlands and is also used by trains covering long distances, for example between the Randstad and Zeeland or Limburg. For travellers, this causes a lot of disruption. Travelling by train around the disruption is possible via Gouda; NS is deploying buses between Rotterdam Centraal and Delft station. <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> of Infrastructure is shocked by the incident. "That this is arson and therefore deliberate I find very objectionable and worrying", she says.

title: AI tips off police about Philadelphia murder case, but its story is nonsense
lead: "I may have information about the murder case", an unknown source wrote to the American police on 18 July. "I can remember seeing someone who fits your description." A tip for the police in the American city of Philadelphia about an unsolved murder case. However, the message did not come from an eyewitness at all, it now turns out. Moreover, the message was not even written by a human: the tip was submitted by artificial intelligence (AI). The American AI company Anthropic tested its AI application Claude on the internet over the past months, in order to develop advanced models. That went wrong, the company confesses. Unclear instructions During that testing phase, the AI model was given a number of restrictions. For example, it was not allowed to create accounts or take harmful actions. The assignment did not say that the AI models had permission to fill in forms on the internet, but that was not explicitly forbidden either. For Claude that was reason enough to submit a tip about a murder case. Which murder case it concerns has not been disclosed. It has also not been disclosed what the purpose of the AI program was with the tip. The AI tip about the murder case already arrived at the police this summer, but Anthropic only shared this week that the tip was fake. "The two-month delay in tracing and reporting the incident is unacceptable", says the Philadelphia police. No data stolen The police say the AI tip was "marked as spam" and that nothing was ever done with the report. Anthropic has reportedly now stopped the tests. According to the police, there are no indications that the AI models had access to the police systems. As far as is known, this is the first time an AI model has passed a false tip on to the police. Anthropic reported the incident this week to the American regulator FTC. Other incidents Anthropic also reported incidents on American government websites to the regulator. The company does not say what exactly it could do there or which websites were involved. However, all parties involved would have been informed. The AI models would also have managed to get around an online paywall. The models did this by modifying website links. Anthropic only shared the incidents with the American regulator at the end of September. "Companies must report incidents with their models immediately and then act quickly and decisively to repair any possible damage", the regulator writes. AI companies want attention Over the past months, AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have massively tested their advanced models. Several incidents also occurred in which the models gained access to places they should not have been at all. The AI companies like to talk about the risks of their newest AI programs in order to stay relevant. The models they warned about earlier usually still reach the market later. This summer it also went wrong in Australia. AI models gained access to various government websites without having permission to do so. OpenAI, the company behind the models, apologised for this. Prime Minister Albanese of Australia called the incidents "unacceptable".

title: Outage at KPN resolved, university hospitals reachable again
lead: Due to an outage at telecom provider KPN, some business customers were hard to reach for hours via the fixed-line telephone. This also applied to a large number of university hospitals, such as in Utrecht, Maastricht, Nijmegen, Rotterdam and Groningen. Around 14.00 KPN reported that the outage that arose overnight has been resolved. KPN says the outage was caused by a fault in the cooling system of one of the network locations. As a result, part of the equipment could no longer be used, because it threatened to overheat. How that fault could arise is being investigated. For security reasons, a KPN spokesperson does not want to say at which location the outage was. Extent unclear According to the telecom company, a small group of business customers were affected. Because of the outage, UMC Utrecht and Wilhelmina Children's Hospital stated on their websites that an alternative telephone number had been opened for urgent matters. UMCG in Groningen also had an alternative number. Emergency number 112 remained fully reachable. In an explanation for patients, Radboud UMC in Nijmegen wrote that callers may have gotten a connection, but then could not hear the hospital employee.

title: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida, southern US prepares for severe weather
lead: Hurricane Isaias has made landfall near the town of Destin in Florida in the United States. Shortly afterward the hurricane weakened, so weather services now describe it as a severe storm. However, the risk of flooding remains considerable in Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis notes. Because of the flood risks and strong gusts, he warns people not to go out on the roads. In Destin streets have been flooded, and in the neighboring city of Pensacola trees have been knocked over, hitting power cables. Videos circulating on social media also show how an entire roof of a hotel is being torn off by the wind. Footage from the town of Crestview, not far from Destin: Storm Isaias has also caused damage in the south of neighboring Alabama. Fallen trees are blocking roads, and power cables there have also been damaged. In total, nearly 800,000 people in Florida and Alabama were without power on Saturday night. People who are still trying to drive to family or friends are too late: because of the fallen trees, it is almost impossible to get from A to B in many places. Although Isaias is no longer an official hurricane, the southern states of America will still experience nuisance this weekend. The expectation is that 10 to 20 centimeters of rain will fall in Florida, Alabama and Georgia this weekend.

title: Prominent figures leave NSC: 'Party has completely strayed'
lead: Former MPs Ilse Saris and Harm Holman have cancelled their membership of Nieuw Sociaal Contract, after Dirk Gotink, the last active NSC politician and a member of the European Parliament, left the party on Wednesday . The immediate reason is the invitation to Mona Keijzer to speak at the NSC party congress today. At the moment she took the floor, about half of the NSC members present left the hall. The party board confirms that this week even more members have expressed their dissatisfaction by cancelling their membership. In an internal message Saris writes: "In my eyes the party has completely strayed from what NSC stood for." Holman tells Nieuwsuur : "NSC was a reasonable centre party on content, but it has degenerated into an increasingly right-wing and populist party. And I don't feel at home in that." Holman has meanwhile rejoined the CDA. The party Nieuw Sociaal Contract was founded three years ago by former CDA member Pieter Omtzigt and won 20 seats in the House of Representatives that same year, out of nowhere. After taking part in a cabinet and Omtzigt's departure for health reasons, the party won 0 seats in the subsequent House of Representatives elections. Since then there has been a exodus of members, and one party figure after another is leaving. Quarrel Nicolien van Vroonhoven, former parliamentary group leader, has also cancelled her membership. She did so after the summer, due to a personal conflict with the party board. "I wrote a letter to the board and I wish them every success. The love between me and the party has cooled. I don't want to say much more about that." Former minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Judith Uitermark has also not been a member of NSC for some time. "The movement I see in the party, I don't feel at home in that." Former state secretary Tjebbe van Oostenbruggen tells Nieuwsuur : "NSC is a closed book for me." Former MP Olger van Dijk is also among those cancelling, and wishes the party "all the best". Amateurish Former campaign leader and former MP Wytske Postma was there from the founding, but she no longer recognises the party of that time. According to her the party is caught up in an internal struggle and has become "a political amateur club". Postma sees the invitation to Mona Keijzer as a lurch to the right, which not everyone supports. The party was founded for good governance, and Keijzer has "a somewhat different style". According to Postma, an dissolution congress today would have been "sensible, however difficult that may be". During today's congress, half of those present left the hall when Keijzer took the floor. Party chairman Ronald de Bruin sees it differently. "We are in a difficult phase and we are a party without a leader. We have invited Mona Keijzer as a guest speaker to look for the common ground." According to a spokesperson for Keijzer, the talk will be about her new political movement Project 2029. Of the former MPs who are still members and whom Nieuwsuur has spoken to, most are not present at today's congress. In the event hall in Breda, about a hundred members were seated this Saturday. The party board ultimately did not survive a motion of no confidence and resigned.

title: Curator left with hundreds of kilos of medicinal weed after bankruptcy of the only Dutch grower
lead: The only legal grower of medicinal cannabis in the Netherlands has been declared bankrupt. This means that around 7,000 people with conditions such as MS and epilepsy will probably no longer be able to obtain medicinal weed from the Netherlands from next year. Meanwhile, the Groningen company Bedrocan has a surplus of hundreds of kilos of medicinal weed that must be sold through the curator. The company, run by the Groningen entrepreneurial family Erkelens, was the first and only company in the Netherlands to receive permission from the government to produce medicinal weed, in 2003. Around seventy people work at the company. Their jobs are at risk. "This has an enormous impact, and the disappearance of Bedrocan is very bitter for the Erkelens family, the staff and the region," says a spokesperson for RTV Noord. The owners do not want to respond to the bankruptcy themselves. Contract terminated The contract between the government and Bedrocan expired at the beginning of this year. Moreover, a change to the Opium Act may be coming. It would make it possible for cannabis producers to sell directly to pharmacies at home and abroad. Bedrocan also tried to prevent the bankruptcy. The bank reportedly would have been willing to advance the largest debt to the energy supplier. It was hoped that the Medicinal Cannabis Bureau, which is now responsible for the production, trade and export of Dutch cannabis, would pay for orders placed in advance. But the company could not reach agreement with the creditors and the BMC. The curator therefore pulled the plug on the company last week. A restart does not seem very realistic. According to the spokesperson, the owner of Bedrocan has "done everything to save what could be saved". Batch of cannabis Hundreds of kilos of medicinal weed, worth millions of euros, are still stored at the company. The curator will try to sell the batch. But because the weed falls under the Opium Act, the curator cannot simply sell it to the highest bidder. Sale is only possible with the cooperation of the BMC. Patients who use medicinal weed for pain and other ailments may have to switch to weed from the coffee shop or medicinal weed from abroad. Hugo Beukeveld (26) previously told the regional broadcaster that this would be "terrible". He has cerebral palsy, and cannabis helps him with pain and muscle spasms. Dutch medicinal weed is standardised. It is always uncertain what effect other weed will have. "That is exactly the strength of Bedrocan's cannabis, its consistency," says Beukeveld.

title: Households will soon pay more for gas, increase in fixed energy contracts
lead: "The heating sometimes comes on already, but we keep in mind that it's expensive. So in the evening a blanket over you or a thick sweater on, that's what you're thinking about now." This customer, like other visitors to the DIY store, is occupied with autumn, which has now truly begun. Many households' heating is coming on again. The chance is high that turning the thermostat will cost more than last year. Because of the war in the Middle East, gas prices have been rising sharply for months. Tom Schuitemaker of comparison site Pricewise sees this too. "The price of gas compared to a year ago is really 40 to 50 cents higher per cubic metre. If you're around an average of 1000 cubic metres, then gas alone amounts to 500 euros per year. Add 250 for electricity, and it adds up quickly." How fast the gas price rose: At the end of October 2025 the average gas price for households was 1.19 euros per cubic metre. Yesterday that price was 1.60 euros. That is an increase of almost 35 percent. On the sites of price comparers an increase is visible in the number of people who want to fix their energy price, also see other providers such as Independer and Overstappen.nl. Notable is that for the first time contracts with a term of several years are slightly cheaper than annual contracts. That is partly because the expectation is that the supply of liquefied gas will increase in the coming years. There are three types of energy contracts. Variable, fixed and dynamic. With a fixed contract you lock in the same energy price for a longer period. For variable contracts there is no end date, but the energy supplier can adjust the price every few months. With a dynamic contract the price changes constantly, every day or even every hour. A fixed annual contract is normally advantageous because you get a discount from an energy company, for example in the form of a welcome bonus. But the 3-year contracts can now compete, says Schuitemaker. "We see that longer contracts are requested 10 times more often than a year ago." Gas price remains high for now: Autumn has only just begun and although temperatures are already dropping somewhat, it will get colder from November. Then demand for gas also increases. For households who want and can control their energy use, a dynamic energy contract is an option, says Gerben Hieminga, senior sector economist energy markets and energy policy at ING. For example, charging your electric car during the day when the sun shines or doing the laundry. For people who want to avoid risks, a fixed contract is an alternative. "If it becomes a cold winter, prices will shoot up. If you want to avoid that risk, you should take a fixed contract." Economist Hieminga expects prices to remain high for now. Schuitemaker of Pricewise thinks so too. Because of the unrest in the Middle East there is less supply for now, and it does not look like that situation will change within a short time.

title: Oil deal or not, Russia attacks residential buildings in Ukraine: 15 dead
lead: Russia may have made agreements with the US on the export of diesel, but in Ukraine the attacks continue. In Russian air attacks in the Zaporizhzhia region, at least fifteen people have been killed, including three children. According to local authorities in the southeast of the country, residential buildings have been bombed. Footage shows the extent of the devastation; entire rooms have collapsed and walls have been blown away. Footage also shows an excavator driving over the rubble to clear debris with a bucket. Rescue services were able to pull people out from under the rubble. At least sixteen people were injured. People are still missing. Earlier this week the Zaporizhzhia region was already attacked. Ukraine reported on Tuesday that five people died in attacks on one of the bridges in the regional capital. Rescue workers also evacuated people after an apartment block was hit and caught fire. In August, Russia attacked the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant several times with drones. The nuclear plant is located a few dozen kilometers from the regional capital. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), radiation levels remained normal after the attacks. Attacks can release harmful radioactive materials. That is why the head of the IAEA called on Russia and Ukraine to show restraint with attacks on nuclear power plants. He calls every attack on nuclear power plants unacceptable. Oil deal Yesterday, US President Trump announced that he is suspending sanctions against Russia, allowing Russians to export diesel again. In 2022, a large part of the world actually stopped buying Russian oil because of the war in Ukraine. The Ukrainian president responds cynically to the oil deal, after overnight attacks on Zaporizhzhia: "Today Russia expressed its thanks for lifting the sanctions on diesel exports. It did so by dropping five glide bombs on residential houses in Zaporizhzhia. Read the article about Trump's suspension of sanctions here: By easing the sanctions, Trump hopes that diesel prices in his own country will fall. In November there are midterm elections in the US, with fuel prices an important issue. The global price of diesel oil rose sharply after the US and Israel started their war against Iran. Oil trade from the Middle East has largely come to a halt, causing a shortage on the market. More than 4.5 years ago, Russia invaded Ukraine, on 24 February 2022. Russian President Putin said he did so to "demilitarize" Ukraine.

title: Nuisance caused by a group of youths in Heerenveen: 'They tie gas cylinders to fireworks'
lead: The municipality of Heerenveen has been dealing with a large group of nuisance-causing youths for weeks. Among other things, they set off fireworks in the evenings. "It is no longer just ordinary fireworks. They tie bottles of turpentine and gas cylinders to them", says council member Nando Vries at Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity> . The council member of Heerenveen Lokaal, the largest faction in the municipal council, says the impact on some residents and entrepreneurs is great. "We had a resident on the line crying because they no longer dare to go out in the evening." Mayor <entity id="person:avine-fokkens-kelder">Avine Fokkens-Kelder</entity> says that a lot is being done behind the scenes to tackle the nuisance. "The municipality and <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> have been in consultation with each other for weeks and a flex team of the police has been deployed." A flex team consists of extra officers who are deployed in a problem-oriented way. " Since Friday we also have concrete names in view." Cat-and-mouse game It has not been announced how many youths are involved. According to Fokkens-Kelder, it was a challenge to map out the nuisance-causers because of the "cat-and-mouse game" between the agencies and the youths. The youths are, among other things, being called to a conversation with the mayor. "But other measures can also be taken, ranging from fines to an area ban", according to the mayor. The mayor also appeals to parents. "I hope people at home have the conversation about what young people get up to in the evenings." The Drenthe town of <entity id="org:gemeente-hoogeveen">Hoogeveen</entity> has also been plagued by nuisance from youths for days. There too, the municipality is intervening. For example, the police can carry out preventive searches in the evenings, cameras are hanging in the centre and a ban on gathering applies.

title: Karbonkel, childhood trauma for millennials, on display in museum: 'Cult phenomenon'
lead: Nightmares and sleepless nights were what schoolchildren were left with in the mid-1990s: villain Karbonkel from the TV series Ik Mik Loreland . The puppet used for the Schooltv programme has now been restored and is on display at the Beeld & Geluid museum in Hilversum. "Teasing, holding back and getting in the way" was the one-eyed troll's strategy in the series. The aim was to teach children in group 3 to read by having them, together with the girl Mik, find the letters that Karbonkel had stolen. The series aired between 1994 and 2002. The series was deliberately made suspenseful: "Research shows that children then keep their attention on it better," explained broadcaster NOT. Made less scary For some children, the teasing monster and his unsightly fish were too much. Children burst into tears in class, had to sit on the teacher's lap or even be taken entirely out of the classroom when the programme was watched. "One of the biggest bogeymen of my generation," a traumatised schoolchild described it years later. "Children dived under the benches out of fear," says another. Another columnist recalls how her mother had to stay in bed with her "because I feared Karbonkel would sneak out from behind my Barbie house and devour me". NOT quickly intervened after the criticism. The music with which Karbonkel appeared was made less threatening, the fish disappeared, and in the third season the puppet was replaced by a less scarily made-up real person. Schools could also request a visit from a Karbonkel puppet to show that it was all fake. A look back with puppeteer Siem van Leeuwen: Beeld & Geluid, where the puppet ended up in storage after the series ended, knew the love-hate relationship this generation had with Karbonkel: visitors often had a strong reaction to the museum piece, and sometimes preferred to keep their distance. When it emerged earlier this year that the puppet was slowly deteriorating, it was decided to restore it. The foam of his body, which slowly decayed from exposure to light, received a kind of sunscreen to protect him better. He was also kept for a while in an airtight bag, so that insects that fed on him died. Insect eggs then disappeared into the restorer's vacuum cleaner. Since today, the restored Karbonkel is on display for a month in his own experience at Beeld & Geluid. He may look a little different from how people remember him: when a human replaced Karbonkel, this puppet was converted into troll boss Bovenbonkel. Before that, his skin was painted grey and he got a little hat. Accompanied Beeld & Geluid now calls its newest resident a cult phenomenon as "one of the scariest television figures from our youth". "For those who dare" can, according to the museum, become "a thrilling reunion". Besides the puppet itself, there are also video footage and photos on display. To prevent Karbonkel from traumatising a new generation, Beeld & Geluid warns that the exhibition has been made "deliberately scary", in a dark room with music, sound effects and flickering light. According to the museum, parents can best judge for themselves whether a visit is suitable for their child, but "we advise children to take part accompanied by an adult".

title: New proposal for billions less EU budget still not sufficient for cabinet
lead: Ireland, as the half-yearly EU presidency, has made a proposal to cut the EU budget for the coming years. Ireland proposes removing 140 billion from it. The upcoming seven-year budget is the subject of much discussion. The Netherlands and five other countries think the European Commission wants too large a budget. The European Commission had proposed a multiannual budget of 1.76 trillion euros (1760 billion). In a letter to EU presidency Ireland, the prime ministers of the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Austria and Finland urged that the budget be cut by hundreds of billions of euros. The countries, which like to call themselves the frugal six, think that less money should go to farmers and poorer regions in the EU. Traditionally those regions receive about two thirds of the budget. The countries instead advocate more investment in security, defence, economic competitiveness, innovation and the fight against illegal migration. In the Irish proposal, 3 percent is removed from the budget proposed by the Commission for, among other things, agriculture, fisheries and poorer regions. Under the heading security, competitiveness and prosperity, the Irish plan instead removes 13 percent of the budget proposed by the Commission. That therefore goes against the wish of the Netherlands, among others, to spend more money on exactly that. Inflation The current budget, which runs until and including 2027, is 1.2 trillion euros. With the Irish proposal, the EU budget still rises by billions to 1.62 trillion. That is an increase of 30 percent, but 8 percent less than the European Commission's proposal. That increase of 30 percent does not mean the European Commission can do much more with it, because inflation makes money worth less. The European Covid debts of 750 billion euros must also be fully repaid by 2050 at the latest. Due to higher interest rates, repayment has become more expensive. The new Irish proposal is part of negotiations that have been ongoing for months and will be discussed next week. On Thursday and Friday the European leaders meet for an EU summit. Netherlands opposes new proposal. The cabinet has already indicated that the new proposal is also insufficient. <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> says in a written response: "The Netherlands cannot agree to this proposal either. The Netherlands wants to see a much larger reduction of the budget together with other countries. We are therefore sending the proposal back immediately." The German government is also not yet satisfied. Chancellor Merz says that "we are still far from" an agreement. Many other EU countries, including Spain and Italy, on the other hand want to hold on to support for agriculture and poorer regions and for more money to go there. In the end, all 27 member states must agree to the budget.

title: Several leaders of Indian cockroach movement arrested at demonstration against Modi
lead: Indian authorities have arrested thousands of supporters of the cockroach movement even before their demonstration got under way. The large square where protests against Prime Minister Modi were to take place was blocked by police vehicles with tear gas installations. The internet was also almost completely shut down, and 45 metro stations were closed. Buses were pulled over to the side of the road to pick up protesters, and the leaders of the protest movement were arrested on a plane upon arrival in Delhi ahead of the protests. See here how the three leaders were arrested on a full plane: "The planned interception by the Delhi police is intended to paralyse the leaders of today's peaceful demonstrations before they even reach the protest site," says the movement. The Indian police say they banned the demonstration because the permit application was submitted too late. In fact, the protests are being nipped in the bud, because the cockroach movement speaks out against a revision of the electoral rolls. If the electoral rolls are indeed amended, activists say millions of Indians risk not being able to vote in future elections. On Thursday, the protests of the cockroach movement were already crushed by the authorities.

title: Wrong-way driver killed in accident on the A2, road closed for hours
lead: In an accident on the A2 near Breukelen, a wrong-way driver died early in the afternoon, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. The identity of the wrong-way driver has not yet been released. According to witnesses, the driver initially drove on the motorway towards Utrecht. At one point the motorist ended up on the other carriageway. At the Breukelen exit he collided with two other cars. Debris was scattered across at least four lanes: The driver of one of those cars was injured. The driver of the other vehicle was unharmed. Motorway closed The motorway towards Amsterdam is closed for investigation. This is expected to last until 18.00 hours. The police are conducting an investigation and are looking for witnesses and dashcam footage. Because of the accident there is a traffic jam of an hour and a half, writes RTV Utrecht. Traffic is being diverted from junction Oudenrijn via the A12, A27 and A1.

title: Five more Palestinians killed in Gaza in Israeli attacks
lead: In Gaza at least five Palestinians have been killed in two separate attacks by the Israeli army. Four people were killed near a shopping centre, and the fifth victim was killed a few kilometres further away. That is what the health authorities in Gaza, which are controlled by Hamas, say. The Israeli army says it carried out the attacks to kill Hamas fighters. It is unknown whether this succeeded. Exactly one week ago, Israel also killed five people in an apartment building in Gaza City. Among them were a mother and her daughter. The Israeli army later said that in that attack it had managed to kill senior Hamas leader Ali Ahmed Al-Amoudi. Gaza under fire Between last night's attacks and last week, Israel repeatedly bombed the Gaza Strip. Last Sunday a Palestinian was killed when Israel attacked a civilian vehicle. Eleven people were injured. Israel said it was trying to kill a Hamas fighter. On Tuesday Israel also attacked targets in Gaza. According to the health authorities in Gaza, two Palestinians were killed in those attacks. The attacks took place near Al Shifa hospital, which Israel destroyed a little over two years ago. Israel says Hamas militants were also the target of these attacks. 74,000 Palestinians dead Yesterday marked exactly one year since Israel and Hamas agreed to a ceasefire. Since then, Israel has killed more than 1467 Palestinians. During that time, Palestinian militants killed four Israeli soldiers. This week Israelis commemorated the victims of the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023. In those attacks, nearly three years ago, about 1200 Israelis were killed and 251 people were taken hostage. Since 7 October 2023, more than 74.000 Palestinians have been killed by Israel in Gaza, including many children. In that period, 175,000 people were also injured. Yellow line Israel occupies more than half of Gaza. A 'yellow line', consisting of yellow-painted concrete blocks, indicates where Palestinians may and may not go. Israel has increasingly moved the markers towards the coast. If Palestinians come near the border, they risk being shot dead by the Israeli army.

title: Train traffic around Schiphol disrupted for hours by power outage
lead: A power outage this afternoon caused problems for train traffic to and from Schiphol. As a result, it was busy at the airport. Also, fewer trains ran between Amsterdam-Zuid, Schiphol and Hoofddorp. Around 15.30 the outage was resolved. The timetable was then restarted. It will still take a while before train traffic runs again according to the normal timetable, says a spokesperson for NS. Also switch fault According to the railway manager ProRail, a power outage occurred in a high-voltage cabinet at Amsterdam Riekerpolder, just before the branch to Amsterdam Lelylaan and Amsterdam-Zuid. "We replaced a defective component, which resolved the outage," said ProRail. The cause of the defect is still being investigated. There were more problems on the rail network today. For example, fewer trains are running between The Hague, Leiden and Rotterdam and between Rotterdam and Dordrecht due to a switch fault. Also, no trains are running between Rotterdam and Delft due to arson this morning at a rail bridge in Delfshaven. It may be sabotage.

title: Jan G. stayed hidden in Overasselt for another twelve hours after escape, this is how he managed to get away
lead: After dozens of armed men had appeared at his gate and shot his bodyguard dead, Jan G. was still in Overasselt for a large part of the day. The convicted drug criminal had fled to family elsewhere in the village. Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> spoke with several sources in Overasselt and, in collaboration with the NOS, reconstructed Jan G.'s flight after the outbreak of violence on 1 September at his house. Not yet suspecting what awaited him that night, the 28-year-old Jan G. stepped into the local supermarket in Overasselt on Monday evening, 31 August. It would be the last time for now that he visited the supermarket. A few hours later, around four in the morning, G. was woken in his chalet on Ewijkseweg by the alarm of his security system. The camera footage showed a group of more than thirty men armed to the teeth. Three of them had earlier that evening tried to break into a house on Honingklaver in Overasselt. A brother-in-law of Jan G. lives here. Alerted by the camera footage, G. fled with his girlfriend and their two young children through a rear exit of the grounds. His parents were still sleeping in a barn elsewhere on the 600 square metre plot. G. and his girlfriend probably walked along a path through a dried-up ditch to hide in the bushes at the edge of a meadow. G. had ordered bodyguard Berry 'urgently'. Meanwhile the armed men had arrived at his home on Ewijkseweg. One of them shot bodyguard Berry, who was sitting in his car at that moment. Shortly before, eye to eye with the group, Berry had called his employer in panic. His employer texted him that he must leave. But by then it was already too late. The bodyguard died of his wounds. Jan G. had ordered bodyguard Berry 'urgently' from a security service two days earlier, after two suspicious persons had walked past his house. Shortly after Berry's death, two police officers who rushed in were also shot. They were seriously wounded. As emergency services flocked in en masse, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> launched a manhunt for the more than thirty suspects. G. and his family were meanwhile picked up by an acquaintance, who took them to his house elsewhere in Overasselt, less than 1200 metres from Ewijkseweg 6. The police rang the doorbell at G.'s house and found his mother there. Once inside the barn, where she and her husband live, the officers saw G.'s father, also a convicted drug criminal. He said: "Get lost, you idiots. Who are you to tell me what to do? I'm not going anywhere at all." The man and the woman were told to stay in the barn and keep the doors closed. Around five in the morning G. contacted the boss of the shot bodyguard and told him that Berry had died. Hiding in Overasselt. While the chaos around Ewijkseweg continued, G. remained in hiding with his family in Overasselt. According to neighbours, the fleeing suspects were unaware that they were running near the house where their target was hiding. Only at the end of the afternoon did a taxi arrive here, after which G. got in with his family and left. The municipality closed the house on Ewijkseweg for a year and imposed an area ban on G. During the day a video surfaced in which criminals demanded compensation from him for a lost consignment of 1283 kilos of cocaine. Visit to collect passports. From that moment on, G. with his family, his parents, and two brothers-in-law with their families had disappeared from the village. Where they are is unclear. In the weeks after the attack, the municipality, under police escort, entered the sealed-off grounds on Ewijkseweg twice more. According to someone in the know, G.'s girlfriend was allowed to briefly return during one of those visits to collect essential items, such as identity documents. The house reportedly had been completely turned upside down during several police investigations. The animals that stayed on the grounds, including horses and large guard dogs, have been placed in boarding facilities. Arrest in Germany. On 18 September G. was arrested in Germany at the request of the Dutch authorities. He is suspected of involvement in the import of cocaine via the port of Dunkirk. According to German police, he was travelling towards the Netherlands via the A44 motorway from the direction of Saxony-Anhalt. Since then G. has been held in a German cell. He still speaks with his lawyer from time to time, but meanwhile a court case looms in Den Bosch. There he will have to answer for his involvement in the cocaine case surrounding Dunkirk, on top of all the other problems that are dogging him. Interviews with those involved. This story is based on a large number of conversations that the authors conducted over the past five weeks with people directly involved in the Overasselt case. All conversations were held on the basis of anonymity. Information from other sources and from official bodies was also used.

title: 18.000 chickens dead in large fire in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen
lead: A very large fire raged this afternoon in a chicken barn in Biervliet in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen. The 18.000 chickens did not survive the fire, a spokesperson for the safety region confirmed to Omroep Zeeland. The fire released a lot of thick, black smoke that could be seen from far away. The Veiligheidsregio Zeeland (VRZ) warned residents to keep windows and doors closed. Cause unknown According to the regional broadcaster, it concerns an organic laying hen barn. The fire broke out around 15.00 hours. The cause is still unknown. There were no people present in the barn. Three fire engines were deployed to fight the fire. A crane is also being deployed to break open the barn. Around 16.30 hours the fire was reported under control. The fire brigade will still be busy for some time extinguishing remaining hot spots.

title: Another attack on educational institution in Poland, third in a week
lead: For the third time in a week, a violent incident has occurred at an educational institution in Poland. This afternoon a woman injured three people at an institution of higher education in the capital Warsaw. How the attack was carried out is not yet known. The police speak of a "dangerous object". The three victims (17, 17 and 24 years old) are not in life-threatening danger. According to Polish media, one of the victims was taken to hospital with cuts. The suspect, a 21-year-old student at the institution, was overpowered by a staff member. Other attacks On Wednesday there was a stabbing at a vocational school in Ostroleka, a town about 120 kilometres north of Warsaw. Five students, two teachers, two bystanders and the perpetrator were injured. A 19-year-old suspect was arrested in the area shortly afterwards. A day later, a 15-year-old killed a caretaker and injured two others in a knife attack at his former school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, just north of the capital. He wore a helmet with a camera during the attack. It is not known whether he was filming at the moment of the attack. Those two incidents prompted the Polish authorities to check almost 50,000 schools for weapons. Since then, more than seventy people have been arrested. For example, a 14-year-old boy was arrested because he had a knife on him. A 16-year-old boy was picked up because he had a butterfly knife in his bag. Other reasons for arrests were threats against peers or threatening attacks on schools. Unrest and measures In app groups on Thursday, a rumour spread among parents that the two attacks had been coordinated and that more attacks would follow on Friday. The Polish government says that so far no evidence has been found that the two attacks are connected. Prime Minister Tusk said on Thursday that he feared copycat behaviour and spoke of an exceptional situation. "For the first time we are dealing with an attacker who had planned to film his attack with a camera helmet." The attacks are causing a lot of unrest. Yesterday, security measures were taken at schools across the country, such as the presence of officers and extra bag checks. Dozens of educational institutions cancelled lessons. There are also reports that parents kept their children at home.

title: Unstable rock formation threatens Swiss village, but a Nepal scenario is not feared
lead: An unstable rock formation threatens to bury the idyllic Swiss mountain village of Kandersteg under millions of cubic metres of rock and ice. Due to global warming, the permafrost is thawing, and it acts as the cement holding the mountains together. As a result, water can get in between the rocks, causing parts to slide. Yet that nightmare scenario does not make the residents particularly nervous. It is worrying, but they are not worried. From Kandersteg, the threatened mountain peak, the Spitze Stei, is clearly visible. The enormous mass of stone casts a shadow over the village of 1300 residents and many times that number of tourists. That entire load will come down someday, that is certain. But how quickly and with how many rocks and how much ice at once is still the question. "We live in the mountains and with nature. Something can always happen. But there is no mountain in Switzerland that is monitored as closely as the Spitze Stei", says one resident. "We have all the information", says another. "If something happens, we know what to do." They still have the recent disaster in Nepal sharply in mind and have certainly not forgotten how a glacier collapse last year destroyed the nearby village of Blatten. But the situation in Kandersteg should not be presented as too dramatic, stresses hotel owner Casimir Platzer of the interest group Spitze Stei. Almost everyone agrees: the authorities and local scientists have this well in hand. That indeed seems to be the case. "At the moment it is small packets coming down", says geologist Cornelia Brönnimann of the canton of Bern. "But we expect that in the future they will be larger packets." She and her colleagues have been closely monitoring the process since 2018 and consider the risk that the entire formation comes down over the village in one go to be very small. Nepal scenario "We still have to see how Kandersteg turns out. Science does not expect a worst-case scenario, but they have made the calculations", says Chandani Bhandari, a natural disaster expert originally from Nepal, of the University of Geneva. "If that scenario comes true, it is truly an enormous disaster, even bigger than in Blatten." In Blatten around 9 million cubic metres of stone and ice came down. In Kandersteg it could even be 15 to 20 million cubic metres, but compared with Blatten this is happening quite slowly. The population is continuously kept informed by the municipality, so that everyone knows what could happen and what to do in case of an evacuation. "That is the way to do it." The destruction in Blatten was immense last year: "The conditions in the mountains are changing very dramatically", stresses glaciologist Mylène Jacquemart of ETH Zurich. The effect of climate change, driven by human CO2 emissions, is very large in the mountains. "The way we see the ice disappear and the permafrost thaw does change the hazards that exist. The art now is to monitor them well and keep track of how everything is changing." Even so, all the scientists interviewed call a Nepal-scale scenario on the Alpine scale very unlikely in Kandersteg, precisely because of that good monitoring. Geologist Brönnimann: "The peak is watched so closely. We assume we will see events early enough and that we have at least two days to warn the population." A disaster in which thousands of people die thus appears to be preventable in the Alps. There are blind spots, but with satellites and other measuring equipment the Swiss can keep enormous areas fairly well under observation. 'Ideal conditions' Compared with her home country, Switzerland has ideal conditions, says Nepalese natural disaster expert Bhandari. "Switzerland is far more developed than our country. There are almost no financial or technical limitations." Nepal, a land of thousands of mountain lakes and many more unstable rock faces, often does not know exactly where the danger lies. Bhandari: "And even when we know, building still takes place along rivers with flood risks, for example. Even with the right knowledge, people can be very distrustful of the government advising them not to do something." Kandersteg does not suffer from that, at least. Hotelier Casimir Platzer, who with his interest group critically follows the municipality in the Spitze Stei file, underlines his confidence in the measurements and the local approach. "The interim results presented to us at the end of June are very promising. They indicate that the risk situation in various places is more favourable than previously assumed."

title: 'Historic moment' in Haarlem: first female bishop in the Netherlands consecrated
lead: A first for the Old Catholic Church in the Netherlands this afternoon. In the Sint Bavokerk, on the Grote Markt in Haarlem, a woman has been consecrated as a bishop for the first time in Dutch history. Erna Peijnenburg may, after the great celebration, call herself bishop of the Old Catholic Church in Haarlem. The Old Catholic Church is a small church community with, by its own account, more than 5000 members. The church is very old, however. It arose in the Netherlands at the beginning of the 18th century as a secession from the Roman Catholic Church. "It is a historic moment," says Peijnenburg. She considers it a tremendous honour. "I am amazed and astonished that I was chosen for this office by colleagues and believers from the diocese." She notices that for many people it is a hopeful event. "For women, but also for men," says the newly consecrated bishop. "I receive many enthusiastic reactions because this is possible. I think it is always lovely when a woman also comes into a group where there were only men before. That has an encouraging effect on the world." Nineteenth bishop. At the end of August the electoral college of the diocese of Haarlem chose her as the new bishop. Before this, Peijnenburg was parish priest in Alkmaar and Enkhuizen. She succeeds Dick Schoon, who retired at the end of June. Peijnenburg is the nineteenth bishop of Haarlem. "Our church chose some time ago to also open the offices to women," she says. "Then women became deacons and priests. Perhaps it was also bound to happen at some point that a woman would be chosen as bishop." Tomorrow at 14.30 hours, during the church service, Peijnenburg will take her seat in her episcopal chair for the first time. Old Catholic Church vs. Roman Catholic Church. Within the Roman Catholic Church women cannot become bishops, but in the case of Peijnenburg it concerns the Old Catholic Church. That is a split from the Roman Catholic Church. She explains that the Old Catholic Church is an independent church. "In terms of content, within the Catholic stream we are closely related to the Roman Catholic Church, but we do have our own way of making decisions." The Old Catholic Church itself describes itself as "a small, self-confident and contemporary faith community that fully stands in the Catholic tradition and at the same time offers a lot of room for a personal interpretation of faith".

title: Injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyad, air traffic at a standstill
lead: An unknown number of people have been injured in attacks on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyad. Two regional officials say the airport has been evacuated after a missile hit a passenger terminal. According to witnesses, ambulances were rushing to the airport. All air traffic to and from King Khalid International Airport has been halted. A source at a local hospital told news agency AFP that dozens of people were injured in the attack. He saw gate 401 of the domestic terminal being hit. "I saw the injured with my own eyes. Everyone ran away." Data from Flightaware shows that at least 225 flights at King Khalid International Airport have been cancelled in the past 24 hours, following the earlier attacks on the airport this week. The airport calls on travelers to contact their airline and check the status of their flight before coming to the airport. Several airlines have already taken measures. Kuwait Airways cancelled all flights to and from Riyad today. Several embassies in Riyhad, including the US embassy, have called on their citizens to avoid the international airport and the surrounding area. Yemen The attack comes two days after the Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked the airport in Riyad. Three Saudis lost their lives in that attack, including a pilot. That international airports are targeted in a series of attacks is exceptional. Earlier this week the Houthis also attacked airfields in the Saudi towns of Jizan, Najran and Abha. These lie a few tens of kilometers from the border with Yemen. Saudi Arabia supports the Yemeni government army, which is fighting the Houthi rebels. Since the start of the large-scale Operation Dawn of Yemen by the Yemeni army last Monday, the Houthis have stepped up their attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia. The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has tightened its guidelines for Saudi airspace. It points to the Houthis' ability to hit targets deeper in the kingdom, including Riyad, and to their "greater focus on aviation infrastructure". The missile and drone attacks, as well as the attempts to intercept them, "increase the risk that civil aircraft will be hit", the agency says. Under fire Meanwhile, the fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces continues. Saudi Arabia is providing air support to the internationally recognized government in Yemen in an attempt to reverse the Houthis' recent territorial gains along the Red Sea. Because of the situation in Yemen, some 200,000 people have fled, including to Djibouti, a small country in the Horn of Africa. The UN migration and refugee agency (IOM) called on countries this week to take action. Saudi Arabia has sought support from the US and other allies, now that its airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure are under fire. This concerns, among other things, sharing intelligence and planning and identifying targets. 'I am not happy' When the American president Trump left the White House yesterday, he was asked about the attacks on the airport in Riyad. "It is not good" and "I am not happy", he told reporters. For now there are no signs of American military support in response to the attacks. The ministers of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> of Saudi Arabia and Oman spoke by phone this week about the importance of "support for diplomatic solutions to reduce tensions in the region". Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, regularly acts as a mediator. But there is not yet any prospect of a solution to the escalation.

title: Christa Pike back in prison, but still receives medical care
lead: A week and a half after the failed execution attempt in the US state of Tennessee, Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital. She is back in prison, American media report. "She will continue to receive medical care in prison and we will keep monitoring her recovery," her lawyers said. "She is grateful to the rescue workers and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances." On Thursday it became known that Pike could walk a little again. Shortly after the failed execution attempt she was already conscious and responsive. The 50-year-old Pike was due to be executed by injection in Tennessee last week, but that failed twice over. She was convicted of murder in 1996. According to the non-profit organisation Death Penalty Information Center, she is the first person to survive her death sentence by injection. From death penalty to life imprisonment? What will happen now is unclear. This week her lawyers argued that Pike has suffered enough. They want the governor of Tennessee to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment without the possibility of release. The investigation into what went wrong is still ongoing. After the failed execution, Tennessee decided to temporarily halt all further executions. A week ago the top official of the state's prison system resigned. This journalist was present at the failed execution: Livestream. There is also a lot of fuss in the US about another execution. Minister Hegseth announced that the execution by firing squad of former military member Nidal Hasan will be livestreamed. President Trump says this has not yet been decided definitively. Minister Hegseth's announcement last Thursday immediately drew a lot of criticism. Former major Hasan shot dead thirteen colleagues at a military base in Texas in 2009. If the execution is indeed broadcast live, it will be the first public execution in the US since 1936.

title: Municipalities want more money for resilience against disasters and threats
lead: Municipalities feel they are receiving too little money from the national government to make themselves resilient against all kinds of threats. These include, for example, cyber and hybrid threats or dangers arising from climate change, such as nature fires. <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity>, chair of the Association of Netherlands Municipalities (<entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity>), says that for the resilience task municipalities need several times what is budgeted in the Miljoenennota. "I assume that in total it really is a matter of hundreds of millions." "<entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has earmarked 35 million for emergency support points and now, in the Miljoenennota, has added a gradually increasing series of 20 to 70 million for digital resilience, socio-societal resilience and continuity alike. But the gap between what municipalities need and what the cabinet is making available is therefore large," says the VNG. <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> also wants more money. The Rotterdam port is often cited as a possible target for threats from Russia. "Resilience goes further than emergency support points, after all. We must also invest in society itself, in a strong social fabric that helps us during an emergency and in the recovery afterwards," says a spokesperson for the municipality. No evacuation facilities. The VNG already has a fairly clear picture of how municipalities would like to deploy extra money. "You can think of neighbourhood emergency plans and training for residents. We still need to talk with the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> about sheltering and evacuation, for which there are now almost no facilities." "Emergency generators, satellite phones and pagers are needed, and the emergency services need many more resources, such as fire engines. The list is too long to list everything." VNG chair Dijksma, who is also <entity id="pos:burgemeester-utrecht">burgemeester van Utrecht</entity>, does have an idea of what needs to happen in her municipality. "We have many vulnerable residents who are not self-reliant, and they do not always have the money to prepare. We also need money for communication tools that we still lack." In Austerlitz, a village in the <entity id="org:gemeente-zeist">gemeente Zeist</entity>, people do not want to wait until municipalities have sufficient resources for safety exercises. Austerlitz lies in the middle of the forest and has few access roads. Because residents feared they would not be able to get away properly in the event of a major forest fire, volunteers set up a 'forest fire working group'. Today the volunteers of the working group practised as if a major forest fire was raging: "I am part of the group of citizens who keep an eye on everything when there is a risk of nature fires," says Robert Schliessler. "We work together with the safety region and train for what happens when our village is threatened." Today Schliessler is also taking part in the first exercise together with the safety region. "We have a WhatsApp group in the village, with six hundred people in it, and they will all be told there when the exercise begins. We have been asking the safety region for this exercise for three years and are super happy that it is finally here," he adds. "By now we work well together with the municipality and the safety region." The idea is that the group of volunteers keeps a close eye on 112 reports and passes on to residents that evacuation is needed. "We do that earlier than the emergency services. We have three locations where people can find each other, and these are determined at the moment we know where the fire is." 'Cannot be financed'. Dijksma is very positive about the exercise in Austerlitz. "It is very important that people also prepare themselves; these kinds of initiatives are gold." Municipal resilience falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security, and <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> is also pleased with the initiative. "I am glad that challenges are being identified and that these kinds of things are being picked up and improved locally." Van Weel can certainly follow the call of the municipalities for more money. "In the Miljoenennota we have designated resilience as an important theme, but our spending will not cover all wishes," he says. "It is an enormous task, so I am not going to say we can do everything at once. We cannot finance that." According to the minister, municipalities can certainly get to work with the money they already receive, for example to work on the resilience of their critical processes. "Ultimately, resilience lies in the communities where people live; municipalities have a very large role in that."

title: Four questions about the diesel deal between the United States and Russia
lead: Yesterday US President Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the US. Much about the agreement is still vague. For example, it is unclear when exactly the diesel will go to the US and what it means for the price Americans pay at the pump. At a later point Russia would supply even larger quantities, rising from 500,000 to 3 million tons. After the news, the future price for diesel fell slightly. What it means for the price in the longer term is still completely unclear. In four questions we explain why the Americans are closing this deal right now and what it means for Ukraine. Why was this deal closed now? Trump already said so in his message announcing the deal: it is about "lower fuel prices for Americans". Since the start of the war in Iran, hardly any oil has been transported through the Strait of Hormuz, which led to a doubling of US diesel prices. It is a headache file for the US president. In less than a month the midterm elections for the US Congress take place. Polls show that Trump is seen as the one to blame for high prices at the pump. That could lead to Republicans losing their majority. To turn the tide, Trump earlier considered a diesel export ban. Now Trump is coming up with the deal with Russia. Correspondent Central and Eastern Europe Christiaan Paauwe: "It is yet another blow for Kyiv regarding the relationship with America, formerly the most important ally. Especially also because of the signal Washington is giving with this. Russia is further pulled out of international isolation with it. Zelensky keeps hammering that Putin can only be forced to talk seriously about peace with further pressure, but this is producing the opposite. Meanwhile, you also see Trump lashing out at Zelensky and saying Ukraine must stop air strikes on the Russian oil industry. Ukraine has made clear that these air strikes, which it describes as "direct sanctions", will not stop unless Russia stops the air strikes on Ukraine. But Putin does not want to stop that, and we don't hear anything more from Trump about it." Can this be done with the sanctions imposed on Russia? President Biden introduced an import ban on Russian oil, natural gas and coal after the invasion of Ukraine. That remained in force under Trump. Last month he still signed a law that makes extensive American sanctions against Russia possible. That law states that the US can impose import duties of up to 100 percent on countries that buy a lot of Russian fuels. Trump is now pushing that law aside: the US Treasury Department has granted a temporary license for the import of Russian diesel. What does this yield Russia and what does it mean for Ukraine? President Zelensky is, to put it mildly, not pleased with Trump's decision. On Telegram he called it a "gift for Putin". According to him, the US is playing into Russia's hands and this has major consequences for the war in Ukraine. According to Zelensky, the Russian war chest is being filled by the deal. He states that "every extra billion dollars Russia can earn is spent on nothing but weapons." According to him, the Russian attacks are indicative of what the purchase of Russian diesel means: "the prolonging of the war, terrorizing ordinary people and destroying infrastructure". Not only in words, but also in deeds, Ukraine shows that the country is angry. For example, a large fire broke out at an oil terminal in the port from which Russia would transport the fuel, in Rostov-on-Don. The suspicion is that this is due to a Ukrainian air strike. The American president has then again emphasized that Ukraine must stop attacks, adding that he thinks Ukraine should get a new leader. How can Russia supply diesel to the US? Russia is a country with enormous oil fields, but itself struggles with a fuel shortage due to Ukrainian attacks on its oil industry. Ukraine regularly carries out attacks on oil refineries in Russia, where crude oil is converted into fuels. This summer that led to queues at petrol stations in all corners of the country. Russia then decided on an export ban for petrol, diesel and kerosene. The Kremlin also concluded a deal with India for the import of fuel. So Russia can probably supply diesel only to a limited extent, but any dollar it earns can be used for producing weapons. Putin's adviser Oesjakov reported yesterday that in the conversation between Putin and Trump, peace talks with Ukraine came up, but that Russia's goals have remained the same. So that means Russia continues the war.

title: Until at least 23.00 no trains between Rotterdam and Delft after arson
lead: No trains will run between Rotterdam and Delft until at least 23.00. The reason is the arson last night at a railway bridge in Rotterdam-Delfshaven. ProRail does not rule out that sabotage is involved. According to the railway manager, it will take until at least Sunday evening before the damage is repaired. Trains may not run on the route again until Monday morning. The railway between Rotterdam and Delft is one of the busiest routes in the Netherlands. It is also used by trains covering long distances, for example between the Randstad and Zeeland or Limburg. For train travellers, this also means a lot of inconvenience tomorrow. Eight-hour check According to ProRail, it is certain that the fire was deliberately started last night. The fire started last night in the technical room. The door to it had been pried open and inside lay smouldering cables. Research shows that 35 cables were damaged. Fifteen of them have burned through completely and must be replaced and re-welded. After replacing all cables, various checks must be carried out to determine whether the trains can run safely again. These checks take about eight hours. Whether sabotage was actually committed on the railway again must still be investigated by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and fire brigade. No one has been arrested yet.

title: Trump lashes out at Zelensky: 'Time for a new president who can make a deal'
lead: President Trump has once again lashed out at Ukrainian president Zelensky. In a conversation with the American press, Trump said it is time for Ukraine to get a new leader. According to him, that leader could then make a deal to end the war with Russia. Trump's jab at Zelensky comes a day after the American president announced that the US will import oil and diesel from Russia . Trump has repeatedly said he thinks Ukraine should stop attacking Russian oil refineries, but right after announcing the deal, Ukraine attacked the port of Rostov-on-Don, which is essential for diesel exports. Speaking to the American press, Trump also claimed that Zelensky has not done enough to end the war. Trump says the new leader of Ukraine should be "someone who can make a deal, something Zelensky never does for some reason". Trump further claimed that the war in Ukraine would never have started if he had been US president at the time. "It started because of incompetence." Ukrainian elections The American president, in his attack on Zelensky, ignores the fact that the Ukrainian constitution states that no elections can be held in wartime. It is not the first time Trump has raised elections in Ukraine. In December he claimed that the Ukrainian government "is using the war to avoid holding elections". His outburst can be seen as reinforcing the message of Russian president Putin. He has repeatedly said Ukraine must hold elections, because Zelensky's term of office ended in 2024. Yet there is also a call from Ukraine itself for elections, but that is not feasible. A poll also shows that a majority of the population believes elections can only come after the war. Diesel deal Kyiv, to the displeasure of the Americans, does not intend to stop attacking the Russian oil industry, because according to Ukraine it is a way to hit the Russian economy and thus the war chest. Zelensky only wants to stop attacking the oil sector if Russia stops its air attacks on Ukraine. Since the start of the war in Iran, diesel prices in the US have doubled, to the displeasure of many Americans. They hold the Trump administration responsible for the high fuel prices. This is also visible in the polls for the American midterm elections in early November. These elections are important for Trump, because he wants to keep a majority in the American Congress. Row in the White House Trump's outburst recalls Zelensky's visit to the White House early last year. Then a meeting between the two presidents and American vice president JD Vance escalated into a heated row. The conversation was supposed to lead to an agreement in principle on the reconstruction of Ukraine, with arrangements on the extraction of raw materials. But Zelensky was insulted by the Americans. He was accused of being "disrespectful". "Either you make a deal, or we walk away from it," said Trump, after the Ukrainian president was told by the Americans that "he has nothing to demand". Zelensky left the White House that day without the agreement having been signed.

title: At least forty dead in Sudan after drone attack on refugee camp
lead: At least forty people have been killed in a drone attack in Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. That is what Emergency Lawyers , an organisation that tracks developments in the civil war in Sudan, reports. According to the organisation, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are behind the attack. The BBC reports that a refugee camp in the southeast of the country was the target. UN aid organisation OCHA says it is shocked by the attack. Most of the victims are women and children. For more than three years now, the RSF has been fighting the government army, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), in Sudan. The war broke out after the leaders of both parties jointly staged a coup and then could not agree on how to divide power. War crimes According to the UN, the civil war in Sudan is the largest humanitarian crisis in the world. Both the RSF and the SAF commit war crimes, but the RSF is seen as the most violent of the two. The violence of the RSF has hallmarks of genocide, the UN concluded. The RSF mainly holds large parts of western Sudan, such as Darfur. The government army controls the east and north, including Khartoum. Millions of Sudanese have been displaced by the violence. NOS op 3 earlier made this video about the war in Sudan:

title: 12 dead and 300 injured in attack on Riyadh airport
lead: The attacks on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh have killed at least twelve people and injured 300. That is what the Saudi civil aviation authorities say. It is therefore the deadliest attack in a Gulf state since the start of the war between the US and Israel with Iran in February. The New York Times reports that the Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for the attack through a senior official. According to him, the attack was retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Yemen, including attacks on civilian infrastructure. King Khalid Airport is the second largest in Saudi Arabia, after the one in Jeddah. The damage to the terminal is now being mapped. There is virtually no photo or video footage available of the airport after the impacts. Air traffic has been halted. These verified images do exist: According to the Saudi authorities, four of the dead are from Saudi Arabia. Two others come from Bangladesh. The other victims come from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Sudan and the Palestinian Territories. The injured have been taken to various hospitals. Since the start of a large-scale offensive by the Yemeni government army last Monday, the Houthis have significantly stepped up their attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia is an ally of Yemen; the Houthis, in turn, are supported by Iran. On Thursday the Houthi rebels already attacked Riyadh airport. Three Saudis died in that attack, including a pilot. Earlier this week the Houthis also bombarded airfields in the Saudi towns of Jizan, Najran and Abha. Secretary-General António Guterres of the United Nations says he is "deeply shocked" by the attack on the airport. "Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must stop immediately", he says.

title: Visitor who enters tiger enclosure killed in attack in England
lead: In a zoo near Doncaster in the north of England, a man has died after being attacked by a tiger. South Yorkshire police received a report at 13.35 hours about a man who had entered the park's tiger enclosure. The tiger then attacked the man, after which he died on the spot. Earlier it was reported that the man had been seriously injured in the attack. Later it turned out that medical staff could not help him. After the incident the park was evacuated. The police say they are aware of footage of the attack being shared online and ask people not to share the footage. Why and how the man ended up in the tiger enclosure is not yet clear. The local police are investigating. Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009 and the tiger enclosure "Land of the Tigers" followed two years later. Photos of the special enclosure of just over two hectares show a raised walkway for visitors and a fence above the area where the tigers can roam freely. Park closed this weekend A spokesperson for the park says the staff are "deeply saddened" by the death of the man. "Our thoughts and sincere condolences go out to the family and loved ones of the person who has died." The police say the tiger was unharmed and there was no danger to the public. The park has been closed since the incident and remains closed today.

title: Four dead in southeastern US as Storm Isaias brings greater risk of flooding
lead: In the southeastern United States, at least four people have died as a result of Storm Isaias. There is also considerable damage, and hundreds of thousands of households lost power. Within hours after Isaias made landfall, nearly 900,000 households were without power, mainly in Florida and Alabama. Two people died when trees fell on their homes. In Florida, a man died of carbon monoxide poisoning from a generator in his garage. A fourth fatality occurred in Alabama in a traffic accident after a tree had fallen onto the road. Isaias has caused major damage, especially along the Gulf Coast of Florida and Alabama. Roofs and facades of buildings were blown away, and trees were uprooted in several places. The storm is moving on through the southeastern United States and may cause problems in Georgia and North and South Carolina. Although Isaias has since weakened and weather services no longer speak of a hurricane but of a severe storm, meteorologists still warn of heavy rainfall that can cause sudden flooding. Oil from emergency stockpile. President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency for Georgia, after this had earlier been done for Florida and Alabama. This allows federal aid to be deployed. The US Department of Energy has made oil from the emergency stockpile available to prevent possible supply problems as a result of the storm.

title: US Department of Justice investigates TV networks after protest against exclusion of journalists
lead: The US Department of Justice has announced an investigation into several news channels that jointly decided to temporarily stop reporting from the White House. It is the latest chapter in a series of clashes between the Trump administration and major news organisations. The channels being investigated are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News. Out of solidarity, they refused to keep following Trump after CNN, MS Now and Politico were temporarily denied access to the White House. Trump accused the three media companies of spreading fake news, but gave no concrete examples for this. The ministry says it will look into whether the channels have violated competition law. A spokesperson for the ministry speaks of a "joint boycott by commercial competitors" that may conflict with the Sherman Act, as the competition law is called in the US. Difficult relationship Trump has long been fighting against media that in his view are not well disposed toward him. For example, since last year he has banned journalists from Associated Press because the American news agency did not adopt Trump's name change for the Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America). He also regularly attacks journalists personally, particularly women. The ministry's investigation centres on the so-called TV pool of the White House. CNN, ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC are part of this permanent TV pool. In it, one channel is designated to provide footage of press conferences and other important moments at the White House and share it with other media.
