title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies at age 34
lead: American actor RJ Mitte, best known from the TV series Breaking Bad , has died at the age of 34. A spokesperson for Mitte told The New York Times. No cause of death has been announced. In Breaking Bad, Mitte played Junior, the teenage son of main character Walter White, a chemistry teacher at a high school who starts making crystal meth to get out of financial trouble. In the series, Junior suffers from cerebral palsy, a movement disorder resulting from brain damage at a young age. Mitte himself also had cerebral palsy. Breaking Bad marked his breakthrough as an actor. The role of Junior "was exactly like my own life", Mitte said in an interview. "Except for the meth." A scene from Breaking Bad with Junior and Walter White: Before Breaking Bad, Mitte had hardly any acting experience. "There is a perfect role for everyone", he told the newspaper The Oregonian in 2010. Besides Breaking Bad (2008-2013), Mitte appeared in lesser-known series such as Switched at Birth (2011) and The Guardians of Justice (2022). He was also active as a representative of organisations such as United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's, which aim to help people with his disability with regard to care and career.

title: Panda cub Lang Yue moves from Ouwehands Dierenpark to China
lead: The two-year-old panda cub Lang Yue will move from Ouwehands Dierenpark in Rhenen to China at the end of this month. This is necessary to sustain the giant panda population, the park said in a statement . Lang Yue was born at Ouwehands in 2024. It is the agreement with the China Wildlife Conservation Association that pandas born outside China move to China before they are four years old. The animals also originally come from China. Since Lang Yue no longer needs her mother after more than two years, the time has now come for her to live independently in China, the park said. Pandas are by nature animals that live alone a lot. Dad and mum stay. Lang Yue's parents Wu Wen and Xing Ya remain in the animal park. They came to the Netherlands in 2017, attracting great interest, as part of the cooperation with China to protect the giant panda. The animals can still have young. In this way, the park hopes to contribute to the survival of the giant panda. At the end of this month, Lang Yue will be bid farewell with a 'fitting ceremony'. China also lends out pandas to strengthen diplomatic relations with countries. This is also called 'panda diplomacy'. Ouwehands Dierenpark in Rhenen is the only Dutch zoo with giant pandas.

title: Person dead in roller coaster accident in US, man was flung out of car
lead: In an accident with a roller coaster in the American state of Georgia, one person has died and several people have been injured. That happened at the Six Flags Over Georgia amusement park, just west of the city of Atlanta. No details about the cause have been released, but eyewitnesses tell local broadcaster WXIA that a man fell out of the Goliath roller coaster. During his fall he came into contact with the roller coaster several times before landing on the ground. The Goliath is a roller coaster that, according to the Six Flags website, is about 60 metres high at its highest point. One ride lasts 3.5 minutes. The top speed is about 113 kilometres per hour. Because of the incident, people were brought down from the roller coaster at great height: The police are investigating how the man could come out of the car. The Goliath in Georgia opened in 2006. In a response, Six Flags has closed nine similar roller coasters at six amusement parks. This is as a precaution, a spokesperson tells American media. "We are deeply saddened by the incident with our guest." X2 roller coaster closed. Last month another Six Flags location, in Southern California, announced that it is going to stop its famous X2 roller coaster. That happened after the company was sued by several people for serious brain damage as a result of the attraction. The company recently reached a settlement with the relatives of a 22-year-old man, who died in 2022 after a ride on the X2.

title: Veilig Thuis reporting point sounds alarm: 'We can no longer handle the work'
lead: A report of domestic violence or child abuse often ends up in a big pile. For years it takes too long before action is taken. Criticism from outside was already there, but now Veilig Thuis itself is sounding the alarm. This is because the number of advice requests and reports keeps rising, situations are becoming more complex, and there are shortages everywhere in care. Each year, tens of thousands of situations in which people may be being abused are picked up too late. According to the organisation, the only solution is for more money to come from the government. Veilig Thuis is the gatekeeper in tackling domestic violence and child abuse. The reporting point gives advice and investigates reports. Especially that investigation takes a lot of time, because people have to be spoken to or information has to be requested from the GP or school. More and more reports. Year after year the number of reports grows. Veilig Thuis is glad about this, because there is more attention for signs of possible abuse. At the same time, there are too many to pick them all up. Last year it concerned 136,000 reports. For just over 90,000 of those reports the organisation was not yet involved with the family, for the others it was. A report must be picked up within five days, the law says. That often does not happen. In recent years about half of the reports have been picked up later. People now have to wait an average of about two months. In some cases it is longer than half a year. "And the outlook for this year gives no hope," says Ida Ouweneel of the board of the Landelijk Netwerk Veilig Thuis. "Normally the waiting list gets slightly smaller in summer, that has not happened now. In autumn there are usually only more reports. We are not getting through it, it can't go on like this anymore." "We do screen all reports that come in," Ouweneel continues. "If there is acute unsafety, there is no waiting list and we pick up the report right away." Abuse in <entity id="org:gemeente-stadskanaal">Stadskanaal</entity>. The inspectorate has been sounding the alarm about waiting times for years. Lawyers also warned when it became known that in Stadskanaal a 6-year-old girl had been seriously abused. Despite reports to Veilig Thuis, the abuse was able to continue. "At this moment we cannot guarantee that we can pick up all signs of unsafety in time," says Ouweneel. "That worries us greatly." Colinda Guiljam, employee at Veilig Thuis in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>, also sees that the pile of reports is growing. "Every day when I boot up the computer, I see the number of reports getting bigger. At the start of this year it was just over 30 reports on the waiting list in Zeeland, now it is nearly 400 reports." Stalled youth care. "An example of such a situation on the waiting list is someone who hears a lot of screaming and yelling of a child from the neighbours," explains Guiljam. "There is a suspicion of child abuse, but you don't know more at that moment. Because of the big increase in other crisis situations, it takes longer than you would like to get clarity about the situation of such a child." Not only the number of reports is rising, the type of situations is also changing, Guiljam sees. "If domestic violence or child abuse is no longer detected early, such a situation becomes harder." Not only Veilig Thuis is getting stuck. In youth care there are shortages and waiting lists everywhere. Children and young people in a vulnerable situation do not get the help they need in time. That in turn leads to more reports at Veilig Thuis. "We are passing reports around," says Ouweneel. "The waiting list at our end is a result of youth care getting stuck. There has to be a turnaround, in which help is brought in much faster." Turnaround set in motion. Five years ago such a plan came about, from the sector, the national government and municipalities. It focuses on more cooperation and must provide an answer to the many different youth care organisations. "We are working on that turnaround, but there is now no money set aside for it at all," says Ouweneel. "We really need that to invest. Besides that, we need money to hire extra people in the short term. 70 million euros is needed for the coming years from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>." <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Minister Sterk</entity> says in a response that it is important to map out where the bottlenecks at Veilig Thuis come from. She will soon talk with aldermen, the Vereniging Nederlandse Gemeenten and Veilig Thuis to see what is needed. Whether extra money will really come, she does not say. Tomorrow and the day after tomorrow there is a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> on the health care budget, which Veilig Thuis falls under.

title: Morning briefing 13/10: Gang member to learn sentence for murder of rapper 2Pac • Pope Leo surgery
lead: Good morning! In the US a former gang member hears what sentence he will get for the murder of rapper 2Pac, and in Rome Pope Leo undergoes surgery for a small lump on his lung. First the weather: today it is cloudy with occasional light rain or drizzle. With a sometimes strong south to southwest wind, mild air is brought in. It will be 17 to 20 degrees, which is warm for the time of year. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? A report of domestic violence or child abuse often ends up in a big pile. For years it takes too long before action is taken. Criticism from outside was already there, but now Veilig Thuis itself is sounding the alarm. This is because the number of advice requests and reports keeps rising, situations are becoming more complex, and there are shortages everywhere in care. Each year, tens of thousands of situations in which people may be being abused are picked up too late. According to the organisation, the only solution is for more money to come from the government. Other news from the night: And then just this: At Albert Heijn, work is not being done at several distribution centres due to a "cybersecurity incident", as the supermarket chain itself calls it. Experts think there is more going on. It has at least consequences for the supply to the stores. Customers sometimes grab wrong, especially in the produce section: Have a nice day!

title: IMF also more optimistic about the Dutch economy: growth of 1.5 percent
lead: The Dutch economy continues to perform relatively well, despite economic and political unrest in the world. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has also revised its expectations. For the Netherlands, economic growth of 1.5 percent is expected this year. Earlier the fund had predicted growth of 1 percent. The <entity id="org:centraal-planbureau">Centraal Planbureau</entity> (CPB) had also already revised its expectations. The CPB is counting on economic growth of 1.6 percent this year and 1.4 percent for next year. The IMF thinks the Dutch economy will grow by 1.3 percent next year. The Netherlands seems to be benefiting from the fact that the German economy is doing better again. The IMF expects growth of 1.3 percent in Germany this year, where 0.7 percent was previously expected. Despite Iran war The IMF thinks the global economy will grow 3.1 percent this year and 3.4 percent next year. According to IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro, it has succeeded in keeping the effects of the Iran war on oil and gas supplies limited. In addition, growth is being driven by the large amount of investment by big tech companies, she says.

title: Germany arrests two suspects over Starlink sabotage in Poland
lead: Two people have been arrested in Germany on suspicion of sabotaging a Starlink installation in Poland. That is what Polish prime minister Tusk announced. He also says he assumes Russia is behind the incident. Three weeks ago a fire was set at the installation in the central Polish region of Masovia. The deputy prime minister of Poland already spoke of sabotage at the time. Now two Turkish nationals have been arrested in Germany at the request of the Polish authorities. According to German media they were arrested in the southwest of the country, at the train station in Nürtingen, near Stuttgart. The installation is owned by state company Exatel and was not completely destroyed in the fire. Prime Minister Tusk calls the arson "another act of hybrid warfare". The Starlink network, operated by Elon Musk's space company SpaceX, is of great importance to Ukraine, among others. The tens of thousands of terminals provide the country with satellite internet, which the army uses for communication on the battlefield and to control drones, for example. Russian sabotage The fire is one of the examples of suspected Russian sabotage in Poland. Last month a Ukrainian train between Kyiv and Warsaw was also attacked by a Russian drone, and last November a railway line was seriously damaged by an explosive. In response, Poland deployed 10,000 soldiers to protect infrastructure in the country. Such sabotage actions have occurred in more European countries in recent months. For example, a fire was set at a defence company in Estonia, and in the German city of Leipzig a drone with explosives was found near a Ukrainian aircraft. Those actions are a test for NATO. The alliance is faced with the dilemma of whether or not to strike back and possibly fuel a larger conflict. Yesterday the NATO supreme commander gave a speech in Warsaw to signal that the alliance stands ready in case of a Russian attack.

title: A full weapons bin after collection drive in Zaanstreek: 'Mostly the knives shock me'
lead: From knives and punching bags to air rifles and swords: a fair number of weapons were handed in during a collection drive in the Zaanstreek this past week. Residents could hand in their weapons last week anonymously at the police station in Zaandijk, without being punished for possessing prohibited weapons. Especially the knives among them worry the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The weapons were handed in during a collection action by the municipalities <entity id="org:gemeente-zaanstad">Zaanstad</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-oostzaan">Oostzaan</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-wormerland">Wormerland</entity>, in cooperation with the police. Firearms were excluded from the action, because they could cause dangerous situations in the collection bin. It is the sixth year in a row that people in the Zaanstreek have been able to hand in their weapons. Concerns about stabbing weapons: The weapons bin in the hall of the police station is so full that the lid can barely close. "About a hundred weapons," estimates a police officer when he tips the bin over. After counting, there turn out to be 86. That is slightly more than last year, when a total of 78 weapons were handed in. Among the items handed in are air rifles, batons, airsoft weapons and samurai swords. The police are mainly worried about the smaller knives, punching bags and other stabbing weapons. These are easy to conceal and can cause serious injury. According to the police, such a collection action is urgently needed, especially in the Zaanstreek. "Because there is a lot of violence, especially with knives among young people," says the police officer to the regional broadcaster NH. "We want all of that taken off the streets." He picks up a machete about half a metre long. There are fake blood stains on the sharp blade. "We see this a lot among young people too," he says. "You can imagine that if you get hit with this, it won't end well." Addressing grandchildren: The action is not only about the number of weapons handed in. The police also want to make people aware of the dangers of possessing weapons and to talk with them about it. This became clear, for example, when an elderly woman came to the police station with a bag full of knives. She had addressed her grandchildren about their possession of weapons. She then brought the knives that this produced to the police. "Those are just good actions," the police officer concludes. All handed-in weapons will be destroyed later.

title: Twelve days without trains between Arnhem and Utrecht due to works
lead: From Tuesday 20 to and including Saturday 31 October, no trains will run on parts of the route between Arnhem and Utrecht. During that period ProRail is working on the track and building a new railway underpass at Wolfheze station. The works will take place in two phases. From 20 to and including Friday 23 October, no trains will run between Driebergen-Zeist and Arnhem Centraal and between Driebergen-Zeist and Rhenen. After that, train traffic between Arnhem Centraal and Ede-Wageningen will stop from Saturday 24 to and including 31 October. NS is deploying replacement buses on the routes. Travellers are advised to travel by train wherever possible, as replacement bus services are expected to be very busy. Those travelling to Utrecht are best advised to make a detour via 's-Hertogenbosch. Travellers with Amsterdam or further as their destination are advised to travel via Deventer. NS recommends planning the journey shortly before departure in the app. Kirow rail crane: For placing the underpass at Wolfheze station, ProRail is using special equipment, including the Kirow rail crane. That is the largest rail crane in the Netherlands. Interested people can come and watch the operation; ProRail has set up "rail viewing locations" for this purpose. If the works proceed according to plan, ProRail will place the railway underpass in the night of Saturday 24 to Sunday 25 October. The station square in Wolfheze will also be rebuilt to make it more accessible for people with mobility difficulties.

title: No extra training places for dentists despite growing shortage
lead: Despite the growing shortage of dentists, no extra training places are being added for students who want to become dentists. That is what a letter to parliament that education minister <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">Rianne Letschert</entity> is sending today to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> shows. According to the minister, expanding the dentistry programme is "very costly" and costs 30.1 million euros every year. With this decision the minister is disregarding the advice of the Capacity Body, an independent foundation that studies how many dentists and other care professionals will be needed in the future. Last December the advisory body recommended raising the number of training places to 386 per year. There are currently 270, and from next year 290. 'Training programmes have enough room' Etienne Verheijck, education director of the dentistry faculty Acta in Amsterdam, is disappointed that the minister is not adopting the advice. "We think this is unwise. We had hoped the advice would be followed, at least in part. Yes, it costs money, but the programmes have the room to train more students." The shortage of dentists is expected to keep growing in the coming years. The Capacity Body has been advising since 2009 to increase the number of training places. Hans de Vries, chair of the dentists' professional organisation (KNMT), calls it "downright worrying" and "incomprehensible" that the minister is ignoring the advice. By doing so, she would block "a structural solution to keep Dutch oral care accessible in the future." More dental hygienists too The minister has, however, decided to train more students as dental hygienists. From the 2027-2028 academic year, 28 additional students may begin the dental hygiene programme, bringing the total to 381. According to the minister, this increase is necessary because more "task delegation" is coming from dentists, so that dental hygienists take over part of dentists' work. The letter to parliament does not state what additional costs this will entail. Foreign dentists In the Netherlands, the dentist shortage is increasingly being met by dentists from abroad. Currently one in four working dentists in the Netherlands was trained abroad, according to figures from the KNMT. In some regions, such as Zeeland, it is already one in two dentists.

title: Pope in hospital for surgery on lung nodule
lead: Pope Leo XIV has arrived at the hospital in Rome where he will undergo surgery on his lung this afternoon. The 71-year-old church leader stepped out of the car that had brought him to the hospital at the beginning of the afternoon and waved to the hundreds of well-wishers who greeted him. The Pope announced on Sunday that a small nodule had been found on one of his lungs during a medical check-up. It will be removed in the hospital. Even if the nodule is malignant, the prognosis is hopeful according to Leo's doctors, because it was detected at an early stage. Week out of the running Leo has been admitted to the Gemelli hospital, where popes are treated more often. The Vatican estimates that he will need to stay there for one week. The Pope's schedule has been cleared up to and including next Tuesday. The hope is that a planned trip to South America next month can still go ahead as planned.

title: Ash dieback hits Groningen: '10 percent of the trees will survive this'
lead: Ash dieback is an increasingly big problem in Groningen. The Groningen municipalities keep a close eye on the sick ash trees, but sometimes face difficult choices. Next to a busy road, for example, a sick ash can lead to dangerous situations, and then it may be felled. On the other hand, the municipalities want enough greenery in the area. Ash dieback is caused by a fungus that spreads through the air. The tree then dies off branch by branch. There is currently no cure for the disease. In 2010, ash dieback was first found in Groningen. In the years that followed, the disease spread quickly, partly because many forests in the Netherlands consist only of ash trees. <entity id="org:zbo-staatsbosbeheer">Staatsbosbeheer</entity> estimates that 80 percent of all ash trees in the Netherlands are affected. Of all those trees, 43 percent are in <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity>. Groningen ranks second with 12 percent in terms of ash density. 'Only 10 percent will survive the disease' "That is because of the damp Groningen soil", says tree expert Bert Plaat of the Bomenstichting to RTV Noord. "The ash loves that, that damp, nutrient-rich soil." Plaat first saw ash dieback in 2015. "In the Kuzemerkooi, a small nature area of about 10 hectares near Niekerk. It is full of ash trees, of which about 90 percent are now infected." The Stichting Groninger Bomenwacht, which checks trees in the province for diseases, carried out a study in 2017 into ash dieback among the Groningen municipalities. At that time, most municipalities estimated that the disease rate was above 50. In some cases the percentage was even between 75 and 100. Plaat: "Just assume that ultimately no more than 10 percent of the ash trees will survive the disease." No direct felling When the fungus is found in ash trees, this does not mean they are immediately felled. Initially, the municipalities place the trees under extra supervision. The ash trees are then checked more often. As long as they pose no direct danger, they remain standing. In general, intervention is faster when the trees stand along a busy road. The risk of a sick ash depends not only on the condition of the tree, but also on the location, says the municipality of Groningen, which has 16,000 ash trees. "Trees in heavily visited locations, such as along roads, cycle paths or walking routes, pose a greater risk to the surroundings than trees in a forest planting." The <entity id="org:gemeente-westerkwartier">gemeente Westerkwartier</entity>, where almost 8,000 ash trees stand, has even decided not to intervene at all in forests. "We do this because dead trees are important in a healthy forest. As dead trees decompose, nutrients return to the soil." Clearing and replanting whole forests When trees have to be felled after all, the municipalities in most cases plant new ones in their place. The <entity id="org:gemeente-midden-groningen">gemeente Midden-Groningen</entity>, where just over 3,700 ash trees stand, is carrying out large-scale forest management in various parks and nature areas. There the ash trees are so affected that the municipality has decided to clear entire sections and replant them, this time with different tree species. "In this way we want to make the new planting less vulnerable to diseases, pests and changing climate conditions", the municipality says. A tolerant tree The municipalities cannot say exactly how much money they are spending on combating ash dieback, because the costs fall under general green space management. Tree expert Plaat has sympathy for the ash in any case. "It is a very tolerant tree", he says. "Compare it to a beech, which is very selfish, nothing is allowed to grow under it. But under an ash, everything can grow and it teems with vegetation."

title: Albert Heijn restarts systems, 'no indications of stolen customer data'
lead: Ahold says it is working on a "controlled restart of certain systems". The parent company of Albert Heijn also says that there are currently no indications that customer data has been stolen in the cyber incident that Ahold has been dealing with since Sunday afternoon. Asked by the NOS which systems are being restarted, Ahold has not yet answered. By the end of the morning it was already clear that Albert Heijn had resumed supplying supermarkets. Since yesterday, work has stopped at part of the distribution centres. As a result, shelves in supermarkets began to empty. "Several distribution centres are currently operational to supply our stores", Albert Heijn writes in a statement. "In addition, we are today deploying extra deliveries in various ways." Albert Heijn does not want to say further what this precisely involves, from which distribution centres deliveries are being made, or which products are concerned. The union CNV confirms the deliveries. "Deliveries are being made from several distribution centres", says board member Jacqueline Twerda. It is unclear which ones exactly. 'Makeshift' The deliveries are not very coordinated, a source familiar with the logistics process tells the NOS. "It really is makeshift. All perishable goods are being driven out, but where they go is random. They simply drive and then see where they can get rid of them." According to Albert Heijn, despite the supply there may still be empty shelves. "We expect that, for example, longer-lasting products, non-food, frozen products and bread will remain more available than certain fresh products, such as vegetables and fruit. We are working hard to fully restore our delivery capacity." Cyber incident Albert Heijn, Etos and Gall & Gall announced yesterday that since Sunday afternoon they have been experiencing a cyber incident. The websites, apps and customer service of the shops are not reachable due to technical problems. Online ordered groceries could not be delivered, and the electronic shelf labels showed incorrect prices yesterday. According to Albert Heijn, the prices are now correct again. "The current Bonus prices are not yet visible here, but the discounts will still be applied at the checkout." The loyalty systems are not working. Albert Heijn does not want to say anything yet about what exactly is going on. "We have preventively shut down our systems to protect them", CEO Margaret Versteden-van Duijn told the NOS yesterday. Sources in the security world report that Albert Heijn has identified suspicious attack traffic on its systems. Today too, it is still not possible to order or have groceries delivered online. The systems that handle this still do not work. The customer service remains unreachable.

title: De Dag podcast: the 'pep talk' from the highest NATO military commander
lead: It is not often that the supreme commander of NATO is in the spotlight. So when it was announced that Alexus Grynkewich would give a speech on the Russia issue, all eyes turned to him. With the speech, he wanted to reassure NATO citizens in a time of hybrid attacks and at the same time give Russia a firm warning. Want to listen? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Don't forget to subscribe. Defence expert Michelle Haas was at the security conference in Warsaw and in the podcast she tells what struck her about the speech and how it landed among those present. "In a room like that, there is afterwards some doubt about its credibility. Because the big elephant was not named", she says, referring to the rapprochement that US President Trump made towards Putin this weekend. He concluded a deal to buy large quantities of Russian diesel, which fills Russia's war chest. Russia expert Helga Salemon watched Russian TV and other media for De Dag to see how the speech was received there. "Even for Putin, the speech by the military commander is a boost." Want to respond? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial team: Judith Kutschenreuter Final editing: Rosanne Sies

title: Remote-controlled robot molests 16-year-old girl in Cologne
lead: A 16-year-old girl in Germany was probably grabbed by the buttocks by a humanoid robot remotely controlled by a teenage boy. The robot then made thrusting movements against the girl, Cologne police report. According to German police, the girl was standing with girlfriends at a street corner around midnight when the 1.20 metre tall robot walked up to her. Shortly afterwards the police received a report of an assault. Police found the suspected perpetrator by a car, tens of metres further on. The robot was in the boot. Assault livestreamed. The 16-year-old boy reportedly broadcast everything live via social media this weekend together with a 19-year-old friend. They reportedly commented on the robot assault. The robot and the phones of the teenage boys, on which the assault may have been livestreamed, have been seized. The police do not say whether the two have been arrested. An investigation is ongoing. Legal grey area. According to a German lawyer whom the German broadcaster WDR spoke to, it could well prove difficult to hold the pair responsible for the assault with a robot. "When the consequences of an action are unpredictable, due to a certain degree of autonomy of a robot, current legislation faces a problem," says lawyer Martin Ebers. "Then liability becomes complicated." Masturbation movements towards police. Earlier in the evening, before the assault, the robot had already been directed to behave riotously. Footage from earlier that day shows the remote-controlled robot making masturbation movements towards an officer in a police car. The police did not intervene at that time.

title: Albert Heijn detected hacker traffic, attack via multiple foreign servers
lead: Albert Heijn is dealing with a hacking attack or a serious attempt at one. Officially, the supermarket chain does not want to say what its "cybersecurity incident" exactly involves, but sources in the security world report that Albert Heijn has identified suspicious attack traffic on its systems. It appears that Albert Heijn's ICT security staff saw suspicious traffic coming in and decided to shut down the ICT systems. In doing so, they managed to prevent the hackers from penetrating the systems further. So far, Albert Heijn has spoken of a "cybersecurity incident" in which parts of the system were shut down "as a precaution". Multiple computer servers The company knows of several computer servers that were used in the attack, the sources who wish to remain anonymous report. They concern computer servers in the United States, Poland, Moldova and Turkey. That means the attackers used multiple computer servers in several countries to attack. Which server they use says nothing about their physical location: it is easy to route internet traffic through a server in another country. "Albert Heijn has apparently identified the hackers' infrastructure, which they used to explore the systems or with which they wanted to steal data from the Albert Heijn systems", says computer security expert Pim Takkenberg, who regularly assists hacked companies. Information shared Albert Heijn has shared information about the hackers' infrastructure with other companies so that they can better secure their systems. Companies generally only do this when they have serious indications that a server was involved in an attack. Albert Heijn's investigation shows that servers of Ahold's American division may also be involved. "That could mean the hackers broke into those servers and used them to attack Dutch systems", says Takkenberg. That is not yet certain. Contact the editors The NOS is investigating the hacking attack at Albert Heijn. Do you work at Albert Heijn or do you have other information and want to contact us? That can be done by email or via Signal: @schellevis.86 "We take the cybersecurity incident very seriously", Albert Heijn said in a written response. "In the interest of the investigation and security, we cannot go into technical details or specific security measures at this time." The company does say that no customer data appears to have been stolen. That Albert Heijn has tracked down specific servers says little about whether the attack succeeded, says cybersecurity expert Joey Fennis. "There are hackers involved in any case, but how successful they were cannot yet be said based on this. It is also possible that Albert Heijn detected them in time." Significant consequences Since Sunday afternoon, Albert Heijn has been dealing with the "cyber incident", which has significant consequences both online and offline. The website, apps and customer service of the stores are unreachable due to technical problems, and ordered groceries were not delivered. Several distribution centers are still down. Albert Heijn said at the end of the morning that it was restocking supermarkets again. A source with knowledge of the logistics system tells the NOS that this is going in a rather unstructured way. Ahold reported this afternoon that it is working on a "controlled restart of certain systems".

title: Netherlands not ready for large military transport in case of war, says Court of Audit
lead: Our roads and rail network are not ready for large military transports during a war on our continent, although under NATO agreements we are expected to play a major role in this. That is the conclusion of the Netherlands Court of Audit after research. At least 9.5 billion euros is needed to meet all requirements for the routes, the so-called military corridors. There is already a large shortfall for the maintenance and construction of bridges, roads and rail in our country: 80 billion according to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, of which already more than 20 billion by 2038 . An additional financial problem comes on top of that for preparing the military transit routes in our country to, for example, Eastern Europe, says the Court of Audit. The advisor to the cabinet finds it worrying that not enough money is being set aside for this in the coming years. According to Barbara Joziasse of the Court of Audit, "choices will have to be made" by politicians. Strategic location Due to our strategic location on the North Sea, our country is a suitable transit country for European transports in wartime, and agreements have been made about this within NATO. It concerns the transport of equipment such as tanks, smaller vehicles or weapon systems for allies. The Court of Audit notes that some vehicles with "exceptional dimensions" cannot currently use the corridors. Where they can, a large part of the infrastructure is due for renewal and replacement. Joziasse: "Outdated bridges already cause problems for freight traffic. That applies even more so to military equipment". Societal impact Our country is also not well prepared for the consequences of large-scale military transports. If war comes and military equipment is transported on a large scale, this will have a major impact on other traffic. That traffic will partly come to a standstill or have to detour, the Court of Audit outlines, with all consequences "for social life". Problems can also arise on the rail network. Transporting wide equipment may mean that not only one track but also an adjacent track cannot be used. The exact routes of the military corridors are confidential. On Friday the cabinet will announce which bridges and roads will be given priority for maintenance or replacement in the coming period. With the billions needed for the military corridors, even more difficult choices are coming. Nevertheless, it is the aim of the cabinet that in the event of war on our continent "large-scale and long-term military transport takes place as efficiently and unhindered as possible", says <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> (VVD) of Infrastructure in a response. According to Karremans, part of the information needed to sharpen the estimate of the final costs of the adjustments is still "in motion" in Europe. When there is more clarity on this, Karremans will further inform <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity>.

title: Tomorrow is the first strike day in regional transport, public transport in big cities still runs
lead: Tomorrow is the first strike day in regional transport, as part of a series of strikes that will continue until Christmas. In large parts of the country, no trains or buses will run from regional carriers Arriva, EBS, Qbuzz, Transdev and Keolis. NS trains will run as normal. Last Friday, the unions FNV and CNV announced that they would strike one day each week because collective labour agreement negotiations had failed. The impact of tomorrow's strike is still unclear. It is up to the employees themselves to decide whether they strike. The carriers have no influence on this. In a number of large cities, transport will at least continue. The carriers in The Hague (HTM) and Amsterdam (GVB) are not taking part in the strike because they provide city transport rather than regional transport. In Rotterdam, the RET trams and metro will run, but the buses will not. In Utrecht, few or no buses and trams are expected to run. Taking to the streets anyway: According to a survey of carriers by news agency ANP, buses and trains are still expected to run, but it will only become clear tomorrow which routes that will be in each region. That depends on how many employees go to work despite the strike. Carriers advise travellers to take cancellations and delays into account. During the national public transport strike at the start of September, it turned out that some bus drivers went to work despite planned strikes. They did not want to leave people who depend on public transport in the lurch. A different day each week: The unions say they understand that the strike is inconvenient for travellers. With the strikes, the unions want wages for employees in the transport sector to rise, staff to get permanent contracts more quickly, and a better early retirement scheme to be introduced. The unions only announce shortly in advance each week which day that week will be a strike day. The intention is for this to be a different day each week, so that carriers cannot prepare with an emergency timetable and travellers are not affected on the same day every week.

title: Dutch national on British sanctions list over deliveries to Russian metal companies
lead: The British government has imposed sanctions on a Dutch national over prohibited deliveries to Russia. It concerns Alexander T., co-owner of the Turkish company Redwing Metal. The Kyiv Independent revealed four months ago that the Turkish company supplies equipment from the European Union to Russian metal companies, which in turn supply missile and fighter jet manufacturers again. In 2023 and 2024, goods worth 5 million dollars were delivered to two factories in Russia. In doing so, Redwing Metal violates export rules, which have been tightened since the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Assets frozen: The British Foreign Secretary says that through his ties to Redwing Metal, the Dutch national is guilty of undermining or threatening the territorial sovereignty of Ukraine. Therefore his assets have been frozen and he receives a British entry ban. The British sanctions package affects a total of 3 persons and 35 entities, including Russian oil companies, shadow fleet tankers, crypto marketplaces and suppliers that supply the Russian army. EU adopts largest sanctions package: Yesterday, sanctions were also again imposed on Russia at EU level. With nearly 1600 persons and companies, this is the most extensive sanctions package the EU has imposed on Russia so far, since the start of the large-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. EU foreign policy chief Kallas said that more than half of the sanctions affect the production chain of ballistic missiles "that Russia uses every day to kill Ukrainian civilians". In addition, 77 people have been punished for organising, working on or participating in "sham elections" in the occupied parts of Ukraine. In total, sanctions have now been imposed on 4500 Russian officials and entities, including President Putin, various oligarchs who support him and Russian politicians.

title: China imposes sanctions on Paraguay and Belize for supporting Taiwan
lead: China has imposed sanctions on ministers from Paraguay and Belize because these countries maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China regards Taiwan as a breakaway province that must, if necessary by force, be reunited with the People's Republic. Ministers from these countries in Central and South America held meetings with their Taiwanese colleagues last month. According to China, they have spread disinformation and interfered in domestic affairs. All assets they may have in China will be frozen, they may no longer enter the country, and they may not cooperate with Chinese individuals and organisations. The penalties imposed on them are mainly symbolic, because government officials from those countries usually do not travel to China or hold assets there. Last twelve: Paraguay and Belize are among the last twelve countries and governments that recognise Taiwan as an independent state. This means, for example, that they have an embassy on the island. The countries have not yet responded to the sanctions from China. The Netherlands does not officially recognise Taiwan, but does cooperate intensively in the fields of economy, technology, science, agriculture and culture. The Netherlands has no official embassy in Taiwan, but does have an office in the capital Taipei where visa applications and consular affairs are handled. 11 countries and 1 <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> that recognise Taiwan. In recent years China has steadily increased military pressure on Taiwan, almost daily sending fighter jets and warships to fly or sail near the island state. China has also campaigned to win over countries that supported Taiwan. For example, Nauru, Honduras and Nicaragua have shifted their loyalty from Taiwan to China in recent years. US and arms deliveries: The US Department of State has stated that the government of President Trump "opposes coercion and aggression by China against countries in our region that use their sovereign rights". "We stand alongside our friends and partners, including Taiwan, to advance our shared prosperity, security and values," a spokesperson for the ministry said. Although the US does not officially recognise Taiwan, since 1979 it has been an important international pillar of support for Taiwan and regularly supplies weapons to the island so it can defend itself against China. In the first year of this Trump administration, more weapons have already been sold to Taiwan than during the four years under President Biden. Bargaining chip: After a visit by Trump to China in May, there appeared to be a shift in that policy. Shortly afterwards, a planned arms delivery was suspended. Trump also called that arms package "a good bargaining chip" after his visit. It was the first time a US president referred to Taiwan as a trump card rather than an ally. Now concern about growing Chinese influence in the US's South American 'backyard' seems to be gaining the upper hand again. China and Taiwan have been governed separately since 1949. That year the Communist Party came to power in Beijing. The defeated Nationalist Kuomintang fled to Taiwan. The island has had its own government ever since.

title: Zelensky: Russia has been ignoring Trump's 'energy truce' for days
lead: Ukraine has abided by the "energy truce" that US President Trump announced on his own on Sunday for the past two days, but Russia has paid no heed to it. That is what Ukrainian President Zelensky says. He points out that his army has not carried out attacks on Russian oil refineries and the energy sector, as Trump wanted. "But Russia has not heeded the American president," Zelensky said. According to the president, the Russians have attacked both power plants and critical infrastructure. "In doing so, they have made it perfectly clear that they have no intention of giving up attacks on Ukraine." Zelensky says that in the past two days alone, nineteen regions in his country have been attacked. Unexpected attack Zelensky also says Ukraine was not warned by its Western partners last night about Russia's launch of five ballistic missiles. They landed in the centre of the capital Kyiv. According to The Kyiv Independent, the air raid alarm only sounded after the missiles had already hit. Western intelligence services help Ukraine in the war against Russia by passing on intelligence to Ukraine about the actions of the Russian army. Last year Trump ordered his services to stop doing so, after he had a quarrel with Zelensky. A week later the quarrel was settled and the intelligence flow resumed. In the Russian attack overnight on an apartment building in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second city, four people were killed and dozens injured: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha said today that there is currently no intelligence stop. That the air raid alarm did not sound in time was, according to him, because Russia had deployed "a special kind of weapon". He did not say what weapons those were. A spokesperson for the Ukrainian air force told The Kyiv Independent that it happens more often that this kind of information does not get through. "We will solve this together with our partners." US pressure on Ukraine increases Trump reported on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed a ceasefire for the energy sector, but Zelensky said he knew nothing about it. He said he was willing to reach an agreement, provided the Russians would also refrain from attacks. A Kremlin spokesperson said that talks were ongoing but gave no further details. In recent days, the long-simmering irritations between Ukraine and the United States have resurfaced. Trump is trying to pressure Ukraine into halting attacks on Russian oil and energy infrastructure so that oil prices in America fall. Diesel prices have doubled since the start of the war in Iran, to the displeasure of many Americans. In three weeks the US goes to the polls for the midterms, in which crucial seats in Congress are at stake. Trump is therefore trying to get prices to fall before then. One example is the deal he concluded on Friday with Russia on the supply of 300,000 tonnes of diesel. School and apartment building under fire At the same time Zelensky says that attacks on the Russian oil sector are an important way to hit Russia economically and thereby pressure it into stopping attacks on Ukraine. For now there is no sign of the latter. Also overnight, a large part of Ukraine was again under fire from, among other things, drones and ballistic missiles, Zelensky says. In an attack on an apartment building in Kharkiv four people were killed. In the past hours 41 people were injured in that region. In addition, a Russian drone hit a school in the northwestern city of Rivne. Twenty people were injured, according to local authorities. One of them is in critical condition in hospital.

title: Van Weel to talk with Halsema about Hamas support at demonstration
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> of Justice is going into talks with <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> of <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> about the pro-Palestinian demonstration on Sunday in the capital. Flags of Hamas were shown there and support was expressed for that Palestinian terrorist organisation. "This went far over my line," said Van Weel this afternoon in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The BBB had brought him to the question hour to give an explanation. That people three years after the massacre of 7 October in Israel glorify Hamas, he finds terrible. "Then you are either naive, malicious or deranged." He thinks the demonstration has been very intimidating for Jewish residents of Amsterdam. Van Weel therefore wants to talk with mayor Halsema. He wants to know from her why she let the protest at the National Monument on the Dam go ahead like that. Face-covering clothing was worn and that can already be a reason to disband a demonstration. She could also have removed the real agitators from among the demonstrators. That did happen in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, for example, at an extreme-right demonstration on the Malieveld. Van Weel wants to consult with the mayors, so that it is handled the same way everywhere in the country. Furthermore he called on the House to deal with a bill against the glorification of terror as quickly as possible. According to the minister, that would make many of the banners and expressions of last Sunday prohibited. Just under the line: Mainly right-wing parties in the House were not satisfied with Van Weel's answers. "It is all weak, weak, weak," said MP Van der Plas of the BBB. She wants the minister to take measures right now. That law already offers that possibility according to her. "Why is nothing being done with it?" But Van Weel maintains that he really needs the amendment of the law to tackle this. The OM decides in most cases not to prosecute, because demonstrators "keep staying just below the line" of what is punishable. "They laugh at us," he said. Last Wednesday a similar protest on the Dam, where support for Hamas was also expressed, was disbanded. But that happened because part of the demonstrators did not follow the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> instructions about the route. Red Line: On 8 November a Red Line demonstration against the situation in Gaza is planned in Amsterdam. JA21 wanted the assurance that no one from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will be present there, because according to MP Nanninga the organisation of the demonstration is linked to Hamas. In the past <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> walked along in a Red Line rally. Van Weel will discuss the matter in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, but he gave no assurance. The <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> states that Hamas has been involved in pro-Palestinian protests in the Netherlands, but according to Van Weel it is not established that this also applies to the Red Line demonstrations. "Of course it is not in itself forbidden to express your support for the Palestinian population. You do have to make that distinction," he said.

title: No place for demonstrators on stadium grounds at AZ match against Israeli club
lead: For fear of confrontations between demonstrators, supporter groups and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the <entity id="org:gemeente-alkmaar">gemeente Alkmaar</entity> has designated a demonstration site outside the stadium grounds ahead of the football match between AZ and the Israeli club Hapoel Be'er Sheva. That Europa League match is being played Thursday evening. Two demonstrations have been registered with the municipality in connection with the match. The demonstrators may not stand at the stadium itself, but may stand across a busy road and roundabout. According to regional broadcaster NH, the new location is along a cycle path that many supporters use to cycle and walk to the stadium before the match. Two pro-Palestinian demonstrations: Mayor Schouten of Alkmaar shared in a letter to the municipal council this morning how the municipality is preparing for the Europa League match on Thursday at the AFAS Stadium in Alkmaar. The letter shows that two pro-Palestinian demonstrations are currently registered with the municipality. The demonstrators had indicated they wanted to stand in front of the doors of the AZ stadium, but neither the municipality nor the police are willing to allow that. Various factors: In the council letter, Schouten writes that she has received signals that Israeli supporters may still come to Alkmaar despite a municipal decision not to admit Israeli supporters. She also takes into account an announcement on social media by various AZ supporter groups in her decision, as well as the chance of a counter-demonstration and the "sentiments in society". The mayor fears confrontations between demonstrators, supporter groups and the police, vandalism, and insufficient safety for visitors if the demonstrations were to take place on the stadium grounds. "On the stadium grounds it is not possible to take sufficient control measures to prevent disorder, and it is not possible to separate visitors to the football stadium from the demonstrators," Schouten writes. The number of demonstrators expected is not known. "At the location where demonstrating is allowed, a safe arrival and departure of demonstrators can be better facilitated," Schouten writes. "It also prevents confrontations with other groups from taking place there." Risk profile: Late last month, Alkmaar decided not to admit Israeli supporters to the match. Although football association UEFA has assigned the Israeli club's supporters a 'medium risk profile', the municipality of Alkmaar classifies the match as a match with a "(very) high risk" "because of the geopolitical context". The municipality explicitly refers to the violent riots around the Ajax-Maccabi Tel Aviv match in 2024. The <entity id="pos:burgemeester-alkmaar">burgemeester van Alkmaar</entity> has been advised by the Amsterdam <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity>. The decision caused outrage in Israel. The Israeli ambassador expressed "serious doubts about the justification" for the decision in a phone call with Schouten. The Israeli foreign minister also raised the matter with his Dutch counterpart Berendsen. Schouten announced yesterday that her decision stands.

title: OM demands six years in prison for man (23) who deployed fake agents 38 times
lead: A man from Nieuwegein is standing trial for committing fraud with fake agents. According to the Public Prosecution Service (OM), the suspect attempted 38 times to gain entry to people's homes via fake agents. It concerns one of the largest fraud cases involving fake agents, the OM says. The 23-year-old man is suspected of being active within a criminal organisation in which he directed people. The group is said to have operated nationwide. According to the OM, the suspect called victims and then passed their addresses on in chat groups. He allegedly used the names "Altijdstroom555" and "kkoeksss" on Snapchat. The man gave instructions to the fake agents within the group. They were then told by the suspect what was present in the house and what they should take. The suspect also gave tips to the fake agents, the OM says. For example, the man allegedly instructed them to "supposedly check locks and fittings in homes". In 26 cases the group succeeded in taking jewellery, cash and bank cards. In the other 12 cases it remained an attempt, the OM says. 'Living like God in France' The man was arrested last summer. He allegedly committed the fraud between September 2024 and July 2025. "In 29 cases the suspect played an active role, in 9 cases the role was passive in nature", says the public prosecutor. The suspect denies a large part of the accusations, but according to the OM there is sufficient and convincing evidence of his criminal activities. "He received a welfare benefit, was under administration, received 40 euros weekly pocket money, but could live like God in France without having to sweat for a boss", according to the public prosecutor. In addition to a prison sentence, the OM also demands that he pay 100,000 euros in damages to victims. Several suspects from the group have already been convicted. The court in Leeuwarden will pronounce its verdict on 30 November.

title: Polish shops remove Halloween accessories from shelves after stabbings
lead: In Poland several retail chains are stopping the sale of certain Halloween accessories following stabbing incidents at schools. Shopkeepers describe the sale as "inappropriate" given the stabbings. Biedronka, with some 3,900 branches one of Poland's largest retail chains, among others, has announced it will remove fake knives and creepy costumes. Children's retail chain Smyk has also said it will no longer sell plastic knives and cleavers, among other items. "Out of concern for the wellbeing of children and young people, we decided yesterday to remove certain Halloween products that may evoke undesirable associations from our range," Biedronka said. In a statement, Smyk indirectly refers to the recent stabbing incidents. "We believe that the presence of such items on the shelves of a store aimed at families is inappropriate under the current circumstances." Third stabbing incident: Last Saturday was the third stabbing incident in just one week at an educational institution in Poland. A 21-year-old woman injured three people: two 17-year-olds and someone aged 24. Earlier, a 19-year-old and a 15-year-old were arrested for two different stabbings in which several people were injured, and at a primary school one person also died. Online rumours also circulated that a "Bloody Friday" would soon take place. The Polish Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said that on Monday about 20,000 police officers had been sent to schools. According to Prime Minister Tusk, the massive deployment has helped bring the situation under control. According to the authorities, the attacks are not linked to an organised group. Instead, the government states that the glorification of violence online is harmful to young people. The Polish government is therefore trying to fast-track legislation that would make it easier to remove harmful online content.

title: Counter-terrorism prosecutor takes over investigation into French school shooter (14)
lead: The French counter-terrorism prosecutor has taken over the investigation into the 14-year-old pupil who shot at a teacher and the head of a secondary school in Aubagne, near Marseille, yesterday. That is what the French news channel BFMTV reports. According to the counter-terrorism prosecutor, there are indications that the boy drew inspiration from the True Crime Community, with which he appears to have ties. This online group glorifies extreme violence, sometimes resulting in violence. A childhood friend who spoke to the French newspaper Le Parisien says the suspect was obsessed with the shooting game Call of Duty and was in social isolation. The boy's father and mother have also been taken in for questioning. The father had numerous weapons lying around the family home, some of which were illegal. According to Le Parisien, the mother was questioned about the boy's plans. Guitar case: According to the authorities, he took a shotgun to school yesterday, hidden in a guitar case. The school staff he shot at were injured but are not in danger of their lives. Sources within the French Public Prosecution Service have told BFMTV that the boy expressed regret. He reportedly said it was revenge on the school staff, although he could not explain how he came to his actions. The headmaster's manner reportedly did not appeal to him.

title: Farmers' organisations want to talk to minister about their own nitrogen proposals
lead: The nitrogen letter from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> should be scrapped and no longer require a permit everywhere. That is what the farmers' organisations united in the Landbouw Alliantie want, and they want to talk with <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity>. This afternoon they presented their plans at the Nieuwspoort press centre in The Hague. The chance that the minister adopts the plans seems minimal. First of all, according to the Landbouw Alliantie, the nitrogen letter from Minister Van Essen of last June must be scrapped. With that slogan, the farmers' organisations toured the country this summer to mobilise farmers for action and to inform them about what is hanging over them. With today's proposals, the alliance hopes to give farmers prospects and to bring the minister around. Compared with Minister Van Essen's nitrogen plans, according to the Alliance, very little is needed to solve the nitrogen problem. Whereas Minister Van Essen sent a thirty-page nitrogen letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> at the start of summer, the alliance mainly focuses on the stalled permit granting. The alliance consists of the farmers' activist group Agractie and the interest groups of dairy and poultry farmers (DDB, NMV and NVP). Paper problem Authorities can currently issue permits for activities that release nitrogen only to a very limited extent. The Landbouw Alliantie's solution is to change the rules so that many businesses no longer need a permit at all. They offer two variants: only businesses within 250 metres of overburdened nature areas need a nitrogen permit, or that obligation applies only to very large emitters. This is not possible under current legislation, emphasises Jan Venneman on behalf of the Landbouw Alliantie. The rules must first be amended. "It is a paper problem, so there must also be a paper solution possible," says Sieta van Keimpema of the DDB about this. Moreover, the Landbouw Alliantie does not want to get straight to work on nature restoration, unlike the minister. The farmers think that the state of nature areas and what is needed for restoration should be reassessed. After that, new management plans must be drawn up. Deterioration of nature "With this proposal you will not unlock permit granting," expects nitrogen expert Jan Willem Erisman of Leiden University, who followed the meeting digitally. He expects the alliance's plans to lead to more nitrogen emissions. "That leads to deterioration of nature, while we have a duty precisely to counter that deterioration." The most important points from the cabinet's nitrogen plans The plans that Van Essen presented at the start of summer include, among other things, stricter standards for livestock farmers and zones around nature areas where only very little nitrogen emission will be allowed in future. In the eyes of the Landbouw Alliantie, those plans will have disastrous consequences for agriculture. The minister holds weekly talks with the farmers' organisations LTO and NAJK. The organisations that make up the Landbouw Alliantie are not at that table. Anger about this also came up during the meetings last summer. Half an hour The minister sent the organisations of the Landbouw Alliantie an invitation two weeks ago, says Jeroen van Maanen, spokesperson for the alliance. "We did not respond to that. We thought: we will first present our plan, and if the minister then has questions, we can explain." Moreover, according to Van Maanen, Van Essen had reserved "only half an hour" for the farmers in his agenda. Far too short, the spokesperson says. "What does a half-hour conversation involve? With ten people you can just about finish a cup of coffee and then you have to leave again." Erik Luiten of Agractie says that a meeting between the minister and the Landbouw Alliantie is now scheduled for next week Thursday. "We then have a quarter of an hour more or so," says Luiten. Harder actions Talks with the minister do not mean that actions are off the table, however. "Willingness to take action among farmers is increasing, including for harder actions," says Van Maanen. Minister Van Essen has responded in writing to the Landbouw Alliantie's proposals. They are not entirely new to him and were also raised earlier in talks with Agractie, he writes. That farmers' organisation and the minister view "fundamentally differently" what is needed to make permit granting possible again, the minister said. Van Essen does not think the Landbouw Alliantie's proposals are a solution, but he is willing to talk with the farmers. "The package of measures as we presented before the summer is and remains the basis for that; we will continue working on that."

title: Lower House: no money for Veilig Thuis, first get things in order
lead: The House of Representatives considers it too early to give the reporting point Veilig Thuis the 70 million euros that its board requested today in an alarming appeal. This is according to a round of inquiries by NOS. First it must finally be examined what exactly is going on there, various factions say. The reporting point says it can no longer handle the large volume of work. VVD, D66, Pro and Groep Markuszower want to know where the problems at Veilig Thuis originated and what <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will do to get things in order. The national Veilig Thuis network is the first and, for many people, often the only reporting point for domestic violence, child abuse, and the prevention of genital mutilation and femicide. The reporting point gives advice and investigates reports. But the waiting lists have been growing for years, and how Veilig Thuis works differs by region. How and how quickly your report is responded to depends on where you live. Reflection The House therefore adopted a motion a year ago, with support from all factions, calling on the cabinet to reflect on "the role, positioning and capacity" of Veilig Thuis. Especially since the cabinet itself emphasises the organisation's public importance. "Time to implement this House motion by the cabinet," says VVD MP Becker now. "More money is not the solution if we do not also fundamentally examine how this has been organised," D66 MP Synhaeve also believes." Pro MP Westerveld holds the previous and current cabinets to account for this. "This is not primarily a matter of money, but of doing what was promised." Situation has worsened In the year since the motion was adopted, the situation has worsened, the emergency appeal from Veilig Thuis shows. After a report, people must wait an average of two months. In some cases it is longer than six months, while by law action must be taken within five days. The board of Veilig Thuis itself speaks of passing reports around, partly due to waiting lists and shortages in youth care. The organisation wants more money to hire extra staff. "If it turns out that extra structural capacity is necessary to guarantee safety, then we must look at that seriously," says Kamerlid Moinat of Groep Markuszower. "But money must fund a solution, not just temporarily cover up the problem."

title: Dijksma positive after Jetten speech
lead: <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity> chair <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity> looks back with a good feeling on the speech that Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> gave on Tuesday at the VNG Annual Congress 2026. title: DigiD manager Solvinity takes a hit, cabinet sticks to ban on takeover

How can it be that such a chatbot cannot answer your question? And if those chatbots don't work anyway, why do companies use them?
